title: Multiplexed RT-LAMP Assays in Handheld Devices for In-Situ Detection of Chikungunya, Dengue, Mayaro, and Zika Viruses.
abstract: Mosquito-borne viruses pose a significant global health challenge, particularly in resource-limited settings where multiple viruses often cause illnesses with similar symptoms that require different treatment. We introduce the first 7-plex reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) assay in a hand-held device capable of detecting the presence of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), dengue virus serotypes (DENV 1-4), Mayaro virus (MAYV), and Zika virus (ZIKV) in a single test. If the result is positive from the single-plex device for the 7-plex assay, 3-plex and 4-plex devices are then used to identify the exact virus within a specimen. In-situ detection is achieved by integrating valve-enabled, paper-based sample preparation with fluorescence detection using a blue LED flashlight as a light source and a yellow plastic film as a filter, allowing visual discrimination between positive and negative samples by the naked eye or by recording images using a smart phone. The detection limits ranged from 2 genome equivalents (GE)/reaction (for ZIKV) to 92 GE/reaction (for DENV-3) across 7 types of viruses when 1 μL of viral RNA was used. We observed 90% overall agreement between the point-of-care (POC) device and lab-based reverse transcription polymerase chain reactions (RT-PCR) when blinded clinical specimens were tested. This assay and device have a potential to address critical surveillance gaps in endemic regions, enabling timely detection of multiple mosquito-borne viruses to guide appropriate clinical management and public health countermeasures in settings where laboratory resources are scarce.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 蚊媒病毒是全球主要的健康负担,特别是在资源有限的环境中,重叠的临床表现使 诊断 和 治疗 变得复杂。该研究解决了对快速、多重检测工具的需求,以区分流行地区的登革热和其他虫媒病毒。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究引入了集成到手持设备中的 7 重 RT-LAMP 检测,用于在一次测试中检测基孔肯雅病毒、登革病毒 血清型 1-4、Mayaro 病毒和寨卡病毒。该检测采用纸质样品制备,通过蓝色 LED 手电筒进行荧光检测,并通过智能手机成像进行视觉辨别。
elements_zh.methods: 原位检测是通过将支持阀门的纸质样品制备与使用蓝色 LED 手电筒和黄色塑料过滤器的荧光检测相结合来进行的,从而能够通过视觉或智能手机记录区分阳性和阴性样品。7 重设备的阳性结果会触发使用 3 重或 4 重设备进行后续测试,以识别特定病毒。
elements_zh.main_results: 当使用 1 μL 病毒 RNA 时,检测限范围从寨卡病毒每个反应 2 基因组 当量到 DENV-3 每个反应 92 基因组 当量。在盲法临床样本中,该床旁检测设备与基于实验室的 RT-PCR 检测结果显示出 90% 的总体一致性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明了多重手持式 RT-LAMP 检测快速原位检测多种蚊媒病毒(包括登革热血清型)的可行性。新颖之处在于第一个集成到便携式设备中的 7 重 RT-LAMP 检测,无需专门设备即可进行视觉辨别。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该检测可以通过及时检测登革热和相关虫媒病毒来解决流行地区的关键 监测 差距,以指导资源有限环境中的临床管理和公共卫生应对措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究报告与 RT-PCR 的一致性为 90%,但没有提供详细的临床敏感性或特异性指标,这限制了诊断性能的信心。由于缺乏全面的验证数据和样本选择的潜在偏差,证据强度中等。

title: Severe Dengue and Dengue–Malaria Coinfection: A Case Series from a Referral Hospital in Montería, Colombia
abstract: Background/Objectives: Severe dengue and dengue–malaria coinfection represent major diagnostic and therapeutic challenges in tropical endemic settings, where overlapping clinical manifestations may delay recognition of deterioration. This study aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of patients with severe dengue, dengue with warning signs, and dengue–malaria coinfection treated at a referral hospital in Montería, Córdoba, Colombia. Methods: A retrospective case series was conducted by reviewing medical records of patients diagnosed with dengue between 2018 and 2023. Cases classified as dengue without warning signs were excluded. The final analysis included patients with dengue-warning signs, severe dengue, and dengue–malaria coinfection. Dengue classification followed the 2009 World Health Organization criteria, and malaria was confirmed by thick blood smear. Sociodemographic, clinical, laboratory, geographic, and outcome-related variables were collected. Descriptive analyses were performed, and selected categorical variables were compared using Fisher’s exact test. Results: Fifty-three patients were included: 25 (47.17%) with severe dengue, 14 (26.42%) with dengue with warning signs, and 14 (26.42%) with dengue–malaria coinfection. Severe dengue was more frequent among females, whereas dengue with warning signs and coinfection predominated in males. Children accounted for the highest proportion of severe dengue cases, while coinfected cases were mainly distributed between childhood and adolescence. Fever was documented in all patients. Edema, elevated hematocrit, severe plasma leakage, and hemodynamic compromise were more frequent among severe dengue cases, whereas myalgia differed significantly across clinical groups. Ten deaths were recorded, six occurring in coinfected patients. Conclusions: Severe dengue and dengue–malaria coinfection are clinically complex conditions with overlapping manifestations and potentially fatal outcomes, highlighting the need for early recognition, differential diagnosis, and close monitoring.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究在转诊医院中检查了 重症登革热、有警告信号的登革热以及登革热-疟疾合并感染,重点关注登革热流行地区的临床和流行病学特征以及诊断挑战。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 回顾性病例系列回顾了 2018 年至 2023 年登革热患者的医疗记录,排除了那些没有警告信号的患者,并使用 WHO 2009 标准对病例进行了分类,并通过厚血涂片确认疟疾;收集社会人口统计学、临床、实验室、地理和结果变量,并使用费舍尔精确检验进行描述性分析。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在53名患者中,重症登革热(47.17%)在女性和儿童中占主导地位,而有预警症状和合并感染的登革热在男性中更为常见,并且分布在儿童和青少年时期;重症登革热 中水肿、血细胞比容升高、严重血浆渗漏和血流动力学损害更为常见,所有患者均出现发热。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究没有对疟原虫种类的合并感染结果进行分层,也没有评估长期后遗症,而且样本量小限制了普遍性;高 死亡率(10 例死亡,6 例合并感染患者)强调了合并感染管理中诊断和治疗的不确定性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 优先考虑流行环境中登革热-疟疾双重感染的差异诊断算法,评估物种特异性疟原虫对登革热严重程度的影响,并针对高危人群(患有 重症登革热 的儿童和双重感染的青少年)实施有针对性的 监测,以减少识别延迟并改善结果。

abstract_zh: 背景/目标:重症登革热 和登革热-疟疾合并感染代表了热带地方病环境中的主要诊断和治疗挑战,其中重叠的临床表现可能会延迟对恶化的识别。本研究旨在描述在哥伦比亚科尔多瓦蒙特里亚一家转诊医院接受治疗的 重症登革热、有警告信号的登革热以及登革热-疟疾合并感染患者的临床和流行病学特征。方法:通过回顾 2018 年至 2023 年间诊断为登革热的患者的病历,进行回顾性病例系列。排除没有警告信号的登革热病例。最终分析包括出现登革热警告体征、重症登革热 和登革热-疟疾合并感染的患者。登革热分类遵循2009年世界卫生组织标准,疟疾通过厚血涂片确诊。收集了社会人口学、临床、实验室、地理和结果相关变量。进行了描述性分析,并使用费舍尔精确检验对选定的分类变量进行了比较。结果:共纳入 53 名患者:25 名(47.17%)重症登革热 患者、14 名(26.42%)具有警告症状的登革热患者、14 名(26.42%)登革热-疟疾合并感染患者。重症登革热 在女性中更为常见,而具有警告信号和合并感染的登革热在男性中占主导地位。重症登革热病例中儿童所占比例最高,而合并感染病例主要分布在儿童期和青春期。所有患者均有发烧记录。重症登革热 病例中水肿、血细胞比容升高、严重血浆渗漏和血流动力学损害更为常见,而肌痛在不同临床组之间存在显着差异。记录了 10 例死亡,其中 6 例发生在合并感染的患者中。结论:重症登革热 和登革热-疟疾合并感染是临床上复杂的病症,具有重叠的表现和潜在的致命结果,强调了早期识别、鉴别 诊断 和密切监测的必要性。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究在转诊医院中检查了 重症登革热、有警告信号的登革热以及登革热-疟疾合并感染,重点关注登革热流行地区的临床和流行病学特征以及诊断挑战。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 回顾性病例系列回顾了 2018 年至 2023 年登革热患者的医疗记录,排除了那些没有警告信号的患者,并使用 WHO 2009 标准对病例进行了分类,并通过厚血涂片确认疟疾;收集社会人口统计学、临床、实验室、地理和结果变量,并使用费舍尔精确检验进行描述性分析。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在53名患者中,重症登革热(47.17%)在女性和儿童中占主导地位,而有预警症状和合并感染的登革热在男性中更为常见,并且分布在儿童和青少年时期;重症登革热 中水肿、血细胞比容升高、严重血浆渗漏和血流动力学损害更为常见,所有患者均出现发热。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究没有对疟原虫种类的合并感染结果进行分层,也没有评估长期后遗症,而且样本量小限制了普遍性;高 死亡率(10 例死亡,6 例合并感染患者)强调了合并感染管理中诊断和治疗的不确定性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 优先考虑流行环境中登革热-疟疾双重感染的差异诊断算法,评估物种特异性疟原虫对登革热严重程度的影响,并针对高危人群(患有 重症登革热 的儿童和双重感染的青少年)实施有针对性的 监测,以减少识别延迟并改善结果。

title: Bulk transcriptomics of peripheral blood mononuclear cells delineates systems-level immune dysregulation in pediatric dengue infection
abstract: Children are disproportionately at a greater risk of developing severe dengue disease, yet the molecular mechanisms driving the heightened susceptibility remains poorly understood. To elucidate the immune determinants of pediatric dengue pathogenesis, we profiled the transcriptomic landscape by performing RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from laboratory-confirmed cases of primary and secondary pediatric dengue, as well as pediatric healthy controls. Differential gene expression (DEG) and pathway analyses were performed to delineate the transcriptional alterations. Pediatric dengue was marked by extensive transcriptional changes with altered expression of genes associated with the complement cascade macrophage-associated genes as well as immune checkpoint molecules. Notably, secondary infection had significant alterations in immune checkpoint molecules and genes associated with macrophage activation, suggesting the onset of immune exhaustion during reinfection. Differences between the primary and secondary dengue cohorts were modest relative to the transcriptional differences observed between either of the groups and healthy controls, with immune checkpoint genes showing the most consistent divergence between the two dengue cohorts. While our initial findings provide early insights into the transcriptional patterns potentially associated with disease outcomes, the dysregulated transcriptomic signatures reported here are preliminary requiring systemic functional validation to determine their biologic role in the immunopathogenesis of pediatric dengue infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Children are disproportionately at greater risk of severe dengue disease, yet the molecular mechanisms driving this heightened susceptibility remain poorly understood, motivating a systems-level investigation of immune dysregulation in pediatric dengue infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: To elucidate immune determinants of pediatric dengue pathogenesis, RNA sequencing was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells from laboratory-confirmed primary and secondary pediatric dengue cases and pediatric healthy controls.
analysis.methods: Differential gene expression and pathway analyses were conducted to delineate transcriptional alterations associated with pediatric dengue infection.
analysis.main_results: Pediatric dengue was marked by extensive transcriptional changes with altered expression of genes linked to the complement cascade, macrophage-associated genes, and immune checkpoint molecules, while differences between primary and secondary infection cohorts were modest.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Secondary infection showed significant alterations in immune checkpoint molecules and macrophage activation genes, suggesting immune exhaustion during reinfection, with immune checkpoint genes showing the most consistent divergence between dengue cohorts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight dysregulated transcriptomic signatures that may inform future studies on immune mechanisms in pediatric dengue and potential targets for diagnostic or therapeutic development.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The dysregulated transcriptomic signatures are preliminary and require systemic functional validation to determine their biological role in pediatric dengue immunopathogenesis, indicating a moderate strength of evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study used RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells to profile transcriptional changes in pediatric dengue infection, comparing primary and secondary cases with healthy controls. Extensive gene expression alterations were observed, including dysregulation in the complement cascade, macrophage-associated genes, and immune checkpoint molecules. Differences between primary and secondary infections were modest, but secondary infections showed significant alterations in immune checkpoint and macrophage activation genes, suggesting immune exhaustion during reinfection. The authors note that these transcriptomic signatures are preliminary and require functional validation to clarify their biological role in disease pathogenesis.

title_zh: 外周血单核细胞的大量转录组学描绘了儿童登革热感染中的系统级免疫失调
source_body_en: Children are disproportionately at a greater risk of developing severe dengue disease, yet the molecular mechanisms driving the heightened susceptibility remains poorly understood. To elucidate the immune determinants of pediatric dengue pathogenesis, we profiled the transcriptomic landscape by performing RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from laboratory-confirmed cases of primary and secondary pediatric dengue, as well as pediatric healthy controls. Differential gene expression (DEG) and pathway analyses were performed to delineate the transcriptional alterations. Pediatric dengue was marked by extensive transcriptional changes with altered expression of genes associated with the complement cascade macrophage-associated genes as well as immune checkpoint molecules. Notably, secondary infection had significant alterations in immune checkpoint molecules and genes associated with macrophage activation, suggesting the onset of immune exhaustion during reinfection. Differences between the primary and secondary dengue cohorts were modest relative to the transcriptional differences observed between either of the groups and healthy controls, with immune checkpoint genes showing the most consistent divergence between the two dengue cohorts. While our initial findings provide early insights into the transcriptional patterns potentially associated with disease outcomes, the dysregulated transcriptomic signatures reported here are preliminary requiring systemic functional validation to determine their biologic role in the immunopathogenesis of pediatric dengue infection.

title: Dengue Fever in Patients with Hematological Malignancies and Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation Recipients: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue is a hyperendemic arboviral infection with a broad clinical spectrum, ranging from self-limited illness to severe disease with shock and multiorgan dysfunction. Immunosuppressed individuals, particularly patients with hematological malignancies and those who have undergone hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT), may be at increased risk for severe manifestations. However, data regarding dengue infection in this population remain limited, especially in endemic settings. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational study including adult patients with hematological malignancies who were diagnosed with laboratory-confirmed dengue virus infection between February and July 2024. Patients were stratified according to prior HCT status (HCT vs non-HCT). Dengue severity was classified according to Brazilian Ministry of Health criteria. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, outcomes, and 30-day overall survival were analyzed. Logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with dengue warning signs. RESULTS: A total of 53 patients were included, of whom 17 (32%) had previously undergone HCT (71% autologous and 29% allogeneic). Age and sex distribution were similar between groups, while underlying hematological diagnoses differed, with multiple myeloma predominating in the HCT group and lymphoma in the non-HCT group (p=0.04). Dengue warning signs were significantly more frequent among HCT recipients (71% vs. 22%, p<0.001), as was grade C dengue (65% vs. Hypotension requiring vasopressor support occurred exclusively in the HCT group (18% vs. Severe thrombocytopenia at diagnosis (platelet count <20,000/μL) was more common in HCT patients (47% vs. In multivariate analysis, male sex (OR 71.11, 95% CI 2.72-1856.76), prior HCT (OR 40.60, 95% CI 2.13-775.62), and platelet count <20,000/μL (OR 17.15, 95% CI 1.47-199.53) were independently associated with dengue warning signs. Thirty-day overall survival was lower in the HCT group (88% vs. CONCLUSIONS: Dengue infection in patients with hematological malignancies, particularly those with prior hematopoietic cell transplantation, is associated with increased disease severity, higher rates of warning signs, and worse short-term outcomes. Heightened clinical suspicion, early diagnostic testing, and close monitoring are essential to improve outcomes in this high-risk population in dengue-endemic regions.

Dengue severity was classified using Brazilian Ministry of Health criteria, and outcomes were analyzed over 30 days. HCT recipients exhibited significantly higher rates of dengue warning signs (71% vs. 22%), grade C dengue (65% vs. 15%), and exclusive occurrence of hypotension requiring vasopressor support (18%). source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Dengue is a hyperendemic arboviral infection with a broad clinical spectrum, ranging from self-limited illness to severe disease with shock and multiorgan dysfunction. Immunosuppressed individuals, particularly patients with hematological malignancies and those who have undergone hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT), may be at increased risk for severe manifestations. However, data regarding dengue infection in this population remain limited, especially in endemic settings. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational study including adult patients with hematological malignancies who were diagnosed with laboratory-confirmed dengue virus infection between February and July 2024. Patients were stratified according to prior HCT status (HCT vs non-HCT). Dengue severity was classified according to Brazilian Ministry of Health criteria. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, outcomes, and 30-day overall survival were analyzed. Logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with dengue warning signs. RESULTS: A total of 53 patients were included, of whom 17 (32%) had previously undergone HCT (71% autologous and 29% allogeneic). Age and sex distribution were similar between groups, while underlying hematological diagnoses differed, with multiple myeloma predominating in the HCT group and lymphoma in the non-HCT group (p=0.04). Dengue warning signs were significantly more frequent among HCT recipients (71% vs. 22%, p<0.001), as was grade C dengue (65% vs. Hypotension requiring vasopressor support occurred exclusively in the HCT group (18% vs. Severe thrombocytopenia at diagnosis (platelet count <20,000/μL) was more common in HCT patients (47% vs. In multivariate analysis, male sex (OR 71.11, 95% CI 2.72-1856.76), prior HCT (OR 40.60, 95% CI 2.13-775.62), and platelet count <20,000/μL (OR 17.15, 95% CI 1.47-199.53) were independently associated with dengue warning signs. Thirty-day overall survival was lower in the HCT group (88% vs. CONCLUSIONS: Dengue infection in patients with hematological malignancies, particularly those with prior hematopoietic cell transplantation, is associated with increased disease severity, higher rates of warning signs, and worse short-term outcomes. Heightened clinical suspicion, early diagnostic testing, and close monitoring are essential to improve outcomes in this high-risk population in dengue-endemic regions.

title: Optimal control strategies for dengue transmission under varying adult prevalence of Wolbachia -carrying mosquitoes: a deterministic mathematical modeling study
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop prevalence-informed post-release dengue control strategies for settings in which Wolbachia-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes have become established through population replacement and to quantify how optimal supplementary intervention intensity and duration vary with adult Wolbachia prevalence, pW. METHODS: A deterministic human-mosquito model was formulated that included Wolbachia-free and Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes and incorporated cytoplasmic incompatibility, maternal transmission, and reduced vector competence. Two bounded supplementary controls were optimized over a 3-year horizon: reduction of effective human-mosquito contact and conventional adult mosquito suppression, represented by increased adult mortality. A quadratic-cost optimal-control problem was solved numerically using the Pontryagin maximum principle and a forward/backward sweep algorithm. Outcomes were compared across representative pW scenarios and prevalence scans. RESULTS: The optimal policies applied high-intensity supplementary control early in the planning horizon and then relaxed control as infection pressure declined. Higher pW reduced the uncontrolled infection burden, decreased the incremental benefit of additional intervention, and shortened the duration of maximum control. In coarse scans with umax=0.30, the terminal dengue infection near-elimination indicator, defined as IH (T)≤10-4 at T=3 years, changed between pW=0.45 and pW=0.50 for all tested cost-weight combinations. A separate refined continuation example demonstrated non-monotonic mean control use and a sharp decrease in cumulative incidence. CONCLUSION: Adult Wolbachia prevalence measured through entomological surveillance may represent an actionable index for post-release dengue management. The identified transition band is a model-based planning indicator, not a universal field threshold or evidence of mosquito population elimination.

analysis.summary_en: This modeling study addressed how to optimize supplementary dengue control strategies in settings where Wolbachia-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes have been established. Using a deterministic human–mosquito model, the authors formulated and numerically solved a quadratic-cost optimal-control problem to determine the intensity and duration of two bounded supplementary interventions—reducing human–mosquito contact and adult mosquito suppression—over a 3-year horizon. Optimal policies front-loaded high-intensity control and tapered it as infection pressure declined. Higher adult Wolbachia prevalence reduced uncontrolled infection burden, decreased the incremental benefit of additional intervention, and shortened the duration of maximum control. A model-based transition band between Wolbachia prevalence of 0.45 and 0.50 was identified as a planning indicator for near-elimination, though the authors caution it is not a universal threshold. The findings suggest adult Wolbachia prevalence could serve as an actionable surveillance index to guide post-release dengue management.

elements_zh.main_results: 最佳政策是尽早实施高强度补充控制,然后随着感染压力下降而放松,较高的沃尔巴克氏体患病率减少了不受控制的感染负担并缩短了最大控制的持续时间。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究将成虫沃尔巴克氏菌 患病率 解释为释放后登革热管理的可行指数,并确定了基于模型的规划中的过渡带,明确指出它不是通用的现场阈值。

abstract_zh: 目的:本研究旨在针对携带沃尔巴克氏体的埃及伊蚊已通过种群更替而定居的环境制定基于 患病率 的发布后登革热控制策略,并量化最佳补充干预强度和持续时间如何随成年沃尔巴克氏体 患病率、pW 的变化而变化。方法:制定了确定性人类蚊子模型,其中包括不含沃尔巴克氏体和携带沃尔巴克氏体的蚊子,并纳入细胞质不相容性、母体 传播 和降低的 媒介 能力。在 3 年范围内优化了两个有界补充控制措施:减少人与蚊子的有效接触和传统的成蚊抑制,以增加成蚊 死亡率 为代表。使用庞特里亚金极大值原理和前向/后向扫描算法对二次成本最优控制问题进行了数值求解。对代表性 pW 场景和 患病率 扫描的结果进行了比较。结果:最优政策是在规划初期实施高强度的补充控制,然后随着感染压力下降而放松控制。较高的 pW 减少了不受控制的感染负担,降低了额外干预的增量效益,并缩短了最大控制的持续时间。在umax = 0.30的粗略扫描中,对于所有测试的成本权重组合,终端登革热感染接近消除指标(定义为T = 3年时的IH(T)≤10-4)在pW = 0.45和pW = 0.50之间变化。一个单独的精炼延续示例演示了非单调均值控制的使用以及累积 发病率 的急剧下降。结论:通过昆虫学 监测 测量的成虫沃尔巴克氏体 监测 可能代表释放后登革热管理的可行指标。确定的过渡带是基于模型的规划指标,而不是通用的现场阈值或蚊子种群消除的证据。

title: Comparative evaluation of machine learning strategies for short-term dengue forecasting in Brazilian capital municipalities.
abstract: Dengue is an arboviral disease of high public health relevance, characterized by pronounced temporal variability, nonlinearity, and recurrent outbreaks, which pose challenges to epidemiological surveillance and decision-making. This study evaluated the performance of machine learning methods for short-term forecasting of the weekly dengue morbidity rate in the 27 Brazilian capital cities, comprising the 26 state capitals and Brasília, Federal District, with horizons up to 4 weeks. Epidemiological, climatic, and socioeconomic data were compiled for these capital cities and used to compare a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) neural network, formulated as a Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) model, and a Gradient Boosting model (CatBoost), implemented using a Direct forecasting strategy with horizon-specific models. Validation was conducted using a walk-forward approach, with evaluation based on absolute error metrics and the coefficient of determination. The results indicated that the GRU architecture presented recurring limitations, including underfitting, temporal lag, and low capacity to anticipate epidemic peaks. In contrast, the CatBoost model demonstrated greater robustness and better adaptation to the variability of epidemiological time series, showing superior performance in most of the analyzed capitals. The findings reinforce that greater architectural complexity does not necessarily imply better operational performance and highlight the potential of ensemble-based methods for short-term epidemiological surveillance applications. These findings contribute to dengue forecasting by showing that, under a common validation framework, ensemble-based strategies may provide greater operational robustness than recurrent MIMO architectures for short-term prediction in heterogeneous epidemiological settings.
authors: Darllan Collins da Cunha E Silva
Pedro Cesar Madureira de Godoy Camargo
Raphael de Vicq Ferreira da Costa

abstract_zh: 登革热是一种与公共卫生高度相关的虫媒病毒疾病,其特点是明显的时间变异性、非线性和复发性,这对流行病学和决策提出了挑战。这项研究评估了机器学习方法对巴西 27 个首府城市(包括 26 个州首府和巴西利亚联邦区)每周登革热发病率短期预测的性能,预测期限长达 4 周。我们为这些首府城市编制了流行病学、气候和社会经济数据,并用于比较门控循环单元 (GRU) 神经网络(制定为多输入多输出 (MIMO) 模型)和梯度提升模型 (CatBoost)(使用特定水平模型的直接预测策略实现)。使用步进方法进行验证,并根据绝对误差指标和确定系数进行评估。结果表明,GRU 架构存在反复出现的局限性,包括拟合不足、时间滞后和预测流行高峰的能力较低。相比之下,CatBoost 模型表现出更强的鲁棒性和更好的适应流行病学时间序列变化的能力,在大多数分析的首都都表现出优越的性能。研究结果强调,更高的架构复杂性并不一定意味着更好的操作性能,并强调了基于集成的方法在短期流行病学 监测 应用中的潜力。这些发现有助于登革热预测,表明在通用验证框架下,基于集合的策略可以比循环 MIMO 架构提供更高的操作鲁棒性,用于异质流行病学环境中的短期预测。

analysis_zh.methods: 使用流行病学、气候和社会经济数据来训练和比较作为多输入多输出 (MIMO) 模型的门控循环单元 (GRU) 神经网络和使用特定水平模型的直接预测策略实现的梯度提升模型 (CatBoost)。
analysis_zh.main_results: GRU 模型反复出现局限性,例如欠拟合、时间滞后和预测流行病峰值的能力较差,而 CatBoost 模型则表现出更强的鲁棒性和对流行病学时间序列变化的更好适应能力。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调,更高的架构复杂性并不能保证更好的性能,并表明基于集合的方法可以为不同环境下的短期登革热预测提供更高的操作稳健性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现有助于开发更可靠的短期登革热预测工具,可以增强流行病学 监测 并支持异构环境中的公共卫生决策。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于前瞻性验证方法,该方法可能无法完全解释所有现实世界的复杂性,并且由于依赖历史数据而没有对 登革病毒 进行直接生物学测试,因此证据是温和的。

title: Detection and structural characterization of bat-associated dengue virus serotype 2: A country-level first detection in Pakistan
abstract: Bats (order Chiroptera) are recognized as reservoirs for diverse zoonotic viruses, including members of the Flavivirus genus. Despite global reports of bat-associated Dengue Virus (DENV), its presence in Pakistan has remained undocumented. This study investigates DENV circulation in bat populations across Islamabad/Rawalpindi, Lahore, Mardan, Swat, and Lower Dir. Fecal samples were screened using CprM-specific primers, yielding 14 amplified viral isolates (BatDENV01-BatDENV14). Phylogenetic analysis confirmed all sequences as Dengue Virus serotype 2 (DENV-2), clustering with bat-associated isolates from Costa Rica (KY461760-KY461769), mosquito-derived (KY461759), and human-derived strains (AY692466, AY692469), and suggests a potential cross-species viral link. Comparative amino acid analysis revealed several substitutions in the CprM region, some of which were unique to the Pakistani bat isolates. These substitutions may reflect host-specific adaptation or regional viral evolution. Secondary structure prediction using SOPMA and PSIPRED indicated conserved α-helices and β-strands, while tertiary modeling via Robetta and visualization in PyMol showed structural homology with reference DENV-2 proteins, and minor modifications were observed. This study provides the first molecular and structural evidence of DENV-2 circulation in Pakistani bats, suggesting a possible ecological link between bat, mosquito, and human transmission cycles. These findings underscore the need for expanded molecular surveillance and structural characterization of bat-associated Flaviviruses to better understand their zoonotic potential and inform public health strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the circulation of Dengue Virus (DENV) in bat populations across Pakistan, addressing the gap in knowledge about the presence of DENV in this region. Bats are recognized as reservoirs for diverse zoonotic viruses, including members of the Flavivirus genus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Islamabad/Rawalpindi, Lahore, Mardan, Swat, and Lower Dir, focusing on bat populations. Fecal samples were collected and screened using CprM-specific primers, resulting in the identification of 14 amplified viral isolates (BatDENV01-BatDENV14).
analysis.methods: The study employed molecular screening using CprM-specific primers to detect DENV in fecal samples. Phylogenetic analysis and comparative amino acid analysis were used to classify and compare the sequences, while secondary structure prediction and tertiary modeling were conducted using SOPMA, PSIPRED, Robetta, and PyMol.
analysis.main_results: Phylogenetic analysis confirmed all sequences as Dengue Virus serotype 2 (DENV-2), clustering with bat-associated, mosquito-derived, and human-derived strains. Comparative amino acid analysis revealed several substitutions in the CprM region, some of which were unique to the Pakistani bat isolates.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest a potential cross-species viral link and highlight the structural homology of the Pakistani bat isolates with reference DENV-2 proteins, indicating possible ecological interactions between bat, mosquito, and human transmission cycles.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide critical molecular and structural evidence of DENV-2 circulation in Pakistani bats, which may inform public health strategies by highlighting the need for expanded molecular surveillance and understanding of zoonotic viral potential.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on fecal samples and the absence of direct host interaction data. However, the molecular and structural evidence is robust, supporting a high confidence assessment in the identification of DENV-2 in bat populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports the first molecular and structural evidence of Dengue Virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) in bat populations across Pakistan, highlighting its potential ecological link with mosquito and human transmission cycles. The research aimed to address the lack of documentation on DENV presence in the region, employing fecal sample screening with CprM-specific primers and phylogenetic analysis. The results showed that all isolates were classified as DENV-2, with unique amino acid substitutions in the CprM region. Structural analysis using SOPMA, PSIPRED, Robetta, and PyMol revealed homology with reference DENV-2 proteins. These findings underscore the importance of expanded molecular surveillance of bat-associated Flaviviruses to better understand their zoonotic potential and inform public health strategies. The evidence is strong, but the study's reliance on fecal samples and lack of direct host interaction data limit its generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查 登革病毒 (DENV) 在巴基斯坦各地蝙蝠种群中的传播情况,弥补对该地区 DENV 存在的了解空白。蝙蝠被认为是多种人畜共患病毒的 储存宿主,其中包括黄病毒属的成员。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在伊斯兰堡/拉瓦尔品第、拉合尔、马尔丹、斯瓦特和下第尔进行,重点关注蝙蝠种群。收集粪便样本并使用 CprM 特异性引物进行筛选,鉴定出 14 种扩增病毒分离株 (BatDENV01-BatDENV14)。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用 CprM 特异性引物进行分子筛选来检测粪便样本中的 DENV。使用系统发育分析和比较氨基酸分析对序列进行分类和比较,同时使用SOPMA、PSIPRED、Robetta和PyMol进行二级结构预测和三级建模。
elements_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析证实所有序列均为 登革病毒 血清型 2 (DENV-2),与蝙蝠相关、蚊子来源和人类来源的菌株聚类。比较氨基酸分析揭示了 CprM 区域的多个取代,其中一些是巴基斯坦蝙蝠分离株所独有的。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明存在潜在的跨物种病毒联系,并强调了巴基斯坦蝙蝠分离株与参考 DENV-2 蛋白的结构同源性,表明蝙蝠、蚊子和人类 传播 循环之间可能存在生态相互作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了 DENV-2 在巴基斯坦蝙蝠中循环的关键分子和结构证据,这可能通过强调扩展分子 监测 的需要和了解人畜共患病毒潜力来为公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖粪便样本且缺乏直接的 宿主 相互作用数据而受到限制。然而,分子和结构证据是强有力的,支持在蝙蝠种群中鉴定 DENV-2 的高置信度评估。

abstract_zh: 蝙蝠(翼手目)被认为是多种人畜共患病毒的 储存宿主,其中包括黄病毒属的成员。尽管全球都有关于与蝙蝠相关的 登革病毒 (DENV) 的报道,但它在巴基斯坦的存在仍然没有记录。这项研究调查了伊斯兰堡/拉瓦尔品第、拉合尔、马尔丹、斯瓦特和下迪尔蝙蝠种群中的登革病毒传播情况。使用 CprM 特异性引物筛选粪便样本,产生 14 个扩增病毒分离株 (BatDENV01-BatDENV14)。系统发育分析证实所有序列均为 登革病毒 血清型 2 (DENV-2),与来自哥斯达黎加的蝙蝠相关分离株 (KY461760-KY461769)、蚊子衍生株 (KY461759) 和人衍生株 (AY692466、AY692469) 聚类,并表明潜在的跨物种病毒联系。比较氨基酸分析揭示了 CprM 区域的多个取代,其中一些是巴基斯坦蝙蝠分离株所独有的。这些替换可能反映了 宿主 特定的适应或区域病毒 进化。使用 SOPMA 和 PSIPRED 进行的二级结构预测表明存在保守的 α 螺旋和 β 链,而通过 Robetta 进行的三级建模和 PyMol 中的可视化显示了与参考 DENV-2 蛋白的结构同源性,并观察到了微小的修改。这项研究提供了巴基斯坦蝙蝠中 DENV-2 循环的第一个分子和结构证据,表明蝙蝠、蚊子和人类 传播 循环之间可能存在生态联系。这些发现强调需要扩展蝙蝠相关黄病毒的分子 监测 和结构特征,以更好地了解其人畜共患潜力并为公共卫生策略提供信息。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查 登革病毒 (DENV) 在巴基斯坦各地蝙蝠种群中的传播情况,弥补对该地区 DENV 存在的了解空白。蝙蝠被认为是多种人畜共患病毒的 储存宿主,其中包括黄病毒属的成员。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在伊斯兰堡/拉瓦尔品第、拉合尔、马尔丹、斯瓦特和下第尔进行,重点关注蝙蝠种群。收集粪便样本并使用 CprM 特异性引物进行筛选,鉴定出 14 种扩增病毒分离株 (BatDENV01-BatDENV14)。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究采用 CprM 特异性引物进行分子筛选来检测粪便样本中的 DENV。使用系统发育分析和比较氨基酸分析对序列进行分类和比较,同时使用SOPMA、PSIPRED、Robetta和PyMol进行二级结构预测和三级建模。
analysis_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析证实所有序列均为 登革病毒 血清型 2 (DENV-2),与蝙蝠相关、蚊子来源和人类来源的菌株聚类。比较氨基酸分析揭示了 CprM 区域的多个取代,其中一些是巴基斯坦蝙蝠分离株所独有的。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明存在潜在的跨物种病毒联系,并强调了巴基斯坦蝙蝠分离株与参考 DENV-2 蛋白的结构同源性,表明蝙蝠、蚊子和人类 传播 循环之间可能存在生态相互作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了 DENV-2 在巴基斯坦蝙蝠中循环的关键分子和结构证据,这可能通过强调扩展分子 监测 的需要和了解人畜共患病毒潜力来为公共卫生策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖粪便样本且缺乏直接的 宿主 相互作用数据而受到限制。然而,分子和结构证据是强有力的,支持在蝙蝠种群中鉴定 DENV-2 的高置信度评估。

title: Severity-associated changes in ICOS, CD27, CD127 and CLA expression and expansion of virus-specific T Cells in acute dengue
abstract: Abstract Background Currently the role of dengue virus (DENV) specific T cell responses in disease pathogenesis and protection are not well understood, including potential differences in those who have obesity. We sought to investigate the functionality and phenotype of T cells in patients with acute dengue fever (DF) or dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF). Methods T cell function was assessed in paired samples (first sample on ≤4 days and second 5-6 since onset of illness) in patients with DF (n=50) and DHF (n=12), using 109 peptides representing CD8+ epitopes and 90 peptides targeting CD4+ T cell epitopes. Phenotypic analysis was in DF (n=21) and DHF patients (n=21), recruited between days 6–8 since onset of illness, by multicolor flow cytometry. Results The frequency of ex vivo IFNγ ELISpot responses to both the CD4+ and CD8+ peptides pools significantly increased from the first (F) to second time (S) point in patients with DF (p 50% of the T cells in 9/21 patients with DHF, with 92.7% expressing CD38. CLA expression was highest in the CD8+CD45RA- of obese individuals, which was significantly higher compared to lean individuals (p=0.01). CD27 and CD127 were both significantly downregulated in patients with DHF compared to DF, with ICOS expression being significantly higher in CD8+ T cells in DHF. Discussion Patients with DHF and obese individuals had impaired T cell functionality compared to patients with DF and lean individuals, with an expansion of activated, skin-homing CD8+ T cells exhibiting downregulation of CD27 and CD127. Our data suggest a contributory role of dysfunctional skin-homing T cells in disease pathogenesis, meriting further investigation.

title_original: Severity-associated changes in ICOS, CD27, CD127 and CLA expression and expansion of virus-specific T Cells in acute dengue

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the insufficient understanding of dengue virus (DENV)-specific T cell responses in disease pathogenesis and protection, particularly in relation to disease severity and obesity. The authors aimed to investigate phenotypic and functional differences in T cells between patients with dengue fever (DF) and dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF).
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a prospective cohort study that enrolled patients with acute DF (n=50) and DHF (n=12), with paired sampling at ≤4 days and 5–6 days post-illness onset for functional assays. Phenotypic analysis was performed in a subset of DF (n=21) and DHF (n=21) patients recruited between days 6–8 post-illness onset using multicolor flow cytometry.
analysis.methods: T cell function was assessed using IFNγ ELISpot assays with 109 CD8+ and 90 CD4+ epitope peptide pools. Phenotypic markers (ICOS, CD27, CD127, CLA) were measured by flow cytometry, and comparisons were made between DF and DHF patients, as well as between obese and lean individuals.
analysis.main_results: IFNγ ELISpot responses to both CD4+ and CD8+ peptide pools significantly increased from the first to the second time point in DF patients. In DHF patients, CD27 and CD127 were significantly downregulated compared to DF, while ICOS expression was higher in CD8+ T cells. CLA expression was highest in CD8+CD45RA- T cells of obese individuals and significantly higher than in lean individuals (p=0.01).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating impaired T cell functionality in DHF and obese individuals, with an expansion of activated, skin-homing CD8+ T cells exhibiting downregulation of CD27 and CD127. They proposed a contributory role of dysfunctional skin-homing T cells in dengue pathogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that phenotypic and functional profiling of T cells could inform risk stratification and targeted immunotherapies in dengue, particularly for severe cases and obese patients. They also highlight the need for further investigation into skin-homing T cell dysfunction in disease pathogenesis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by a small sample size, particularly for DHF (n=12), and lacked longitudinal follow-up beyond the acute phase. The evidence strength is moderate due to potential confounding by obesity and unmeasured host factors, and the generalisability is constrained by the single-centre design.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated T cell responses in acute dengue, comparing patients with dengue fever (DF) and dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF). Functional assays showed increased IFNγ ELISpot responses over time in DF patients, while DHF patients exhibited significant downregulation of CD27 and CD127 and higher ICOS expression in CD8+ T cells. Obese individuals had higher CLA expression in CD8+CD45RA- T cells compared to lean individuals. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of impaired T cell functionality in DHF and obesity, suggesting a role for dysfunctional skin-homing T cells in disease pathogenesis. The study highlights potential avenues for risk stratification and immunotherapeutic targeting in dengue, though limitations include small sample size and single-centre design.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了对疾病 发病机制 (DENV) 特异性 T 细胞反应和保护的认识不足,特别是与疾病严重程度和肥胖相关的问题。作者旨在研究 登革热 (DF) 和登革出血热 (DHF) 患者 T 细胞的表型和功能差异。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究,入组了急性 DF (n=50) 和 DHF (n=12) 患者,并在发病后 ≤4 天和 5-6 天配对采样进行功能测定。使用多色流式细胞术对发病后 6-8 天期间招募的 DF (n=21) 和 DHF (n=21) 患者亚组进行表型分析。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 IFNγ ELISpot 测定法对 109 个 CD8+ 和 90 个 CD4+ 表位肽池评估 T 细胞功能。通过流式细胞术测量表型标记物(ICOS、CD27、CD127、CLA),并对 DF 和 DHF 患者以及肥胖和瘦个体之间进行比较。
elements_zh.main_results: DF 患者的 IFNγ ELISpot 对 CD4+ 和 CD8+ 肽库的反应从第一个时间点到第二个时间点均显着增加。在 DHF 患者中,与 DF 相比,CD27 和 CD127 显着下调,而 CD8+ T 细胞中 ICOS 表达较高。肥胖个体的 CD8+CD45RA-T 细胞中 CLA 表达最高,并且显着高于瘦个体 (p=0.01)。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the insufficient understanding of dengue virus (DENV)-specific T cell responses in disease pathogenesis and protection, particularly in relation to disease severity and obesity. The authors aimed to investigate phenotypic and functional differences in T cells between patients with dengue fever (DF) and dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF).
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This was a prospective cohort study that enrolled patients with acute DF (n=50) and DHF (n=12), with paired sampling at ≤4 days and 5–6 days post-illness onset for functional assays. Phenotypic analysis was performed in a subset of DF (n=21) and DHF (n=21) patients recruited between days 6–8 post-illness onset using multicolor flow cytometry.
analysis_en.methods: T cell function was assessed using IFNγ ELISpot assays with 109 CD8+ and 90 CD4+ epitope peptide pools. Phenotypic markers (ICOS, CD27, CD127, CLA) were measured by flow cytometry, and comparisons were made between DF and DHF patients, as well as between obese and lean individuals.
analysis_en.main_results: IFNγ ELISpot responses to both CD4+ and CD8+ peptide pools significantly increased from the first to the second time point in DF patients. In DHF patients, CD27 and CD127 were significantly downregulated compared to DF, while ICOS expression was higher in CD8+ T cells. CLA expression was highest in CD8+CD45RA- T cells of obese individuals and significantly higher than in lean individuals (p=0.01).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating impaired T cell functionality in DHF and obese individuals, with an expansion of activated, skin-homing CD8+ T cells exhibiting downregulation of CD27 and CD127. They proposed a contributory role of dysfunctional skin-homing T cells in dengue pathogenesis.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that phenotypic and functional profiling of T cells could inform risk stratification and targeted immunotherapies in dengue, particularly for severe cases and obese patients. They also highlight the need for further investigation into skin-homing T cell dysfunction in disease pathogenesis.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by a small sample size, particularly for DHF (n=12), and lacked longitudinal follow-up beyond the acute phase. The evidence strength is moderate due to potential confounding by obesity and unmeasured host factors, and the generalisability is constrained by the single-centre design.

source_body_en: Abstract Background Currently the role of dengue virus (DENV) specific T cell responses in disease pathogenesis and protection are not well understood, including potential differences in those who have obesity. We sought to investigate the functionality and phenotype of T cells in patients with acute dengue fever (DF) or dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF). Methods T cell function was assessed in paired samples (first sample on ≤4 days and second 5-6 since onset of illness) in patients with DF (n=50) and DHF (n=12), using 109 peptides representing CD8+ epitopes and 90 peptides targeting CD4+ T cell epitopes. Phenotypic analysis was in DF (n=21) and DHF patients (n=21), recruited between days 6–8 since onset of illness, by multicolor flow cytometry. Results The frequency of ex vivo IFNγ ELISpot responses to both the CD4+ and CD8+ peptides pools significantly increased from the first (F) to second time (S) point in patients with DF (p 50% of the T cells in 9/21 patients with DHF, with 92.7% expressing CD38. CLA expression was highest in the CD8+CD45RA- of obese individuals, which was significantly higher compared to lean individuals (p=0.01). CD27 and CD127 were both significantly downregulated in patients with DHF compared to DF, with ICOS expression being significantly higher in CD8+ T cells in DHF. Discussion Patients with DHF and obese individuals had impaired T cell functionality compared to patients with DF and lean individuals, with an expansion of activated, skin-homing CD8+ T cells exhibiting downregulation of CD27 and CD127. Our data suggest a contributory role of dysfunctional skin-homing T cells in disease pathogenesis, meriting further investigation.

title: Prior Dengue Virus Exposure is Associated with Enhanced Zika Virus-Specific ADCC Activity in a Longitudinal Human Cohort
abstract: Abstract Background Prior dengue virus (DENV) infection is common in regions affected by Zika virus (ZIKV) and may shape immune responses to subsequent ZIKV infection. Although cross-reactive neutralizing and disease-enhancing antibodies have been extensively studied, the effect of prior DENV immunity on antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) responses to ZIKV remains unclear. Methods Longitudinal serum samples were obtained and analyzed from a prospective cohort of 46 PCR-confirmed ZIKV cases enrolled at two U.S. sites between 2016-2018 (follow-up visits 6-409 days). ZIKV cases were classified as DENV-experienced (n=13) or DENV-naïve groups (n=33) based on detection of DENV neutralizing antibodies at baseline. ZIKV-specific ADCC activity was measured using a natural killer cell cytotoxicity assay. Results DENV-experienced individuals had significantly higher peak ZIKV-specific ADCC responses (geometric mean titers [GMT] 15,104 vs 1,819; P 80 days, AUC 953,694 vs 182,004; P=0.0037). Peak ZIKV ADCC magnitude did not correlate with peak DENV or ZIKV antibody neutralizing titers, and ZIKV neutralization efficiency at the time of peak ZIKV ADCC did not differ between groups. However, ZIKV ADCC normalized to ZIKV IgG was significantly higher among DENV-experienced individuals (GMT 2,230 vs 735.6; P=0.0107). Conclusions Prior DENV infection was associated with greater ZIKV-specific ADCC magnitude, despite similar ZIKV neutralization, suggesting that prior DENV exposure shapes Fc-mediated flavivirus immunity beyond neutralization. Future studies are needed to assess the clinical implications of these antibodies in immunopathology and protection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of prior dengue virus (DENV) infection on antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) responses to Zika virus (ZIKV) in a longitudinal human cohort. Serum samples from 46 PCR-confirmed ZIKV cases were analyzed, with participants classified as DENV-experienced or DENV-naïve based on baseline DENV neutralizing antibodies. ZIKV-specific ADCC activity was measured using a natural killer cell cytotoxicity assay. Results showed that DENV-experienced individuals had significantly higher peak ZIKV-specific ADCC responses compared to DENV-naïve individuals, despite similar ZIKV neutralization efficiency. The study suggests that prior DENV exposure may shape Fc-mediated immunity to ZIKV beyond neutralization, which has implications for understanding flavivirus immune responses and their potential impact on immunopathology and protection. The evidence is strong, but the observational design limits the ability to establish causality.

title_zh: 先前的 登革病毒 暴露与纵向人类 队列研究 中寨卡病毒特异性 ADCC 活性的增强有关
source_body_en: Abstract Background Prior dengue virus (DENV) infection is common in regions affected by Zika virus (ZIKV) and may shape immune responses to subsequent ZIKV infection. Although cross-reactive neutralizing and disease-enhancing antibodies have been extensively studied, the effect of prior DENV immunity on antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) responses to ZIKV remains unclear. Methods Longitudinal serum samples were obtained and analyzed from a prospective cohort of 46 PCR-confirmed ZIKV cases enrolled at two U.S. sites between 2016-2018 (follow-up visits 6-409 days). ZIKV cases were classified as DENV-experienced (n=13) or DENV-naïve groups (n=33) based on detection of DENV neutralizing antibodies at baseline. ZIKV-specific ADCC activity was measured using a natural killer cell cytotoxicity assay. Results DENV-experienced individuals had significantly higher peak ZIKV-specific ADCC responses (geometric mean titers [GMT] 15,104 vs 1,819; P 80 days, AUC 953,694 vs 182,004; P=0.0037). Peak ZIKV ADCC magnitude did not correlate with peak DENV or ZIKV antibody neutralizing titers, and ZIKV neutralization efficiency at the time of peak ZIKV ADCC did not differ between groups. However, ZIKV ADCC normalized to ZIKV IgG was significantly higher among DENV-experienced individuals (GMT 2,230 vs 735.6; P=0.0107). Conclusions Prior DENV infection was associated with greater ZIKV-specific ADCC magnitude, despite similar ZIKV neutralization, suggesting that prior DENV exposure shapes Fc-mediated flavivirus immunity beyond neutralization. Future studies are needed to assess the clinical implications of these antibodies in immunopathology and protection.

title: Dengue outbreaks in China during 2005-2023: a systematic analysis
abstract: Objectives Dengue fever is a major global public health concern. While China has not yet established stable, local transmission of the disease, imported cases frequently lead to local dengue epidemics throughout the year. This paper aims to outline the characteristics of dengue outbreaks in China between 2005 and 2023. Methods We collected literature on dengue in China from various databases and extracted relevant data for analysis. This data included patients’ sociodemographic characteristics, serotype composition, and clinical manifestations, which we then summarized and compared, evaluating the relationship between dengue virus (DENV) serotypes and clinical manifestations, and analyzing the monthly and regional distribution patterns of dengue fever cases based on case data obtained from the China Public Science and Health Data Center (CPC). Results In the included studies, the ratio of male to female was approximately 1:1, The age group with the highest proportion of dengue patients is those aged 30 to 39. Their occupations were predominantly business service, and the predominant serotype of the infection was DENV-1, followed by DENV-2. The major clinical signs and symptoms in dengue patients were fever, asthenia, and headache. Patients infected with DENV-1, 3 were associated with some specific clinical phenotypes. Dengue cases typically peak between September and October each year. Although these cases are primarily concentrated in the southern regions of China, there is a noticeable trend of increasing incidence in northern areas over time. Conclusions This study offers an in-depth examination of the molecular epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and the seasonal and geographic distribution of dengue cases in China from 2005 to 2023. The findings provide valuable insights for future research on dengue epidemics.

abstract_zh: 研究目的 登革热 是全球重大公共卫生问题。尽管中国尚未建立稳定的本地性 传播,但输入性病例频繁导致全年登革热流行。本研究旨在梳理 2005 年至 2023 年中国登革热 暴发 的特征。研究方法 从多个数据库收集中国登革热相关文献,提取患者社会人口学特征、血清型构成及临床表现等数据并进行分析。分析内容包括 登革病毒(登革病毒,DENV)血清型与临床表现的关联,以及基于中国公共科学与健康数据中心(CPC)病例数据的月度和区域分布模式。研究结果 纳入研究中,男性与女性患者比例约为 1:1;30 至 39 岁年龄组登革热患者占比最高;职业以商业服务业为主;主要感染血清型为 DENV-1,其次为 DENV-2。登革热患者主要临床表现为发热、乏力和头痛。DENV-1、3 感染与某些特定临床表型相关。登革热病例每年通常在 9 至 10 月达到高峰。病例主要集中在中国南方地区,但北方地区病例呈现随时间增长的趋势。研究结论 本研究深入分析了 2005 年至 2023 年中国登革热病例的分子 流行病学、临床特征及季节性与地理分布。研究结果为未来登革热流行研究提供重要参考。

title: PEMBERANTASAN SARANG NYAMUK (PSN) - DEMAM BERDARAH DENGUE (DBD) DI DESA BANING KOTA DAN JERORA, SINTANG (Implementation of Mosquito Nest Eradication - Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever)
abstract: The Dengue Fever Eradication Movement (PSN-DBD) is a crucial activity aimed at combating the transmission of Dengue Fever (DBD). This action aims to break the chain of mosquito breeding and its transmission. A mosquito-free, clean, and healthy environment will decrease the incidence and mortality rates due to DBD. The objective of this community engagement initiative is to reduce DBD cases in Sintang Regency through collaboration and cross-sectoral efforts. The activity spans two periods and involves monitoring larval sites, providing abate, and conducting fogging under the supervision of the Tanjung Puri Sintang Community Health Center. The results of this initiative include fogging and abate application in all households in RT 14 Rw 03 Baning Kota Sintang, along with abate application at Rainwater Collection Points (PAH). In Jerora Village, fogging was conducted at SMPN 7 Sintang, TK Santa Yohana, the Jerora Village Office, SDN 12 Sintang, and the Panca Setya Sintang School Complex (Elementary, Junior High, Vocational High School, and High School). Sustainable activities and monitoring evaluations are necessary to support this initiative by increasing community awareness and concern for PSN-DBD. Recommendations include continuous surveillance, community education campaigns, and intersectoral collaboration to sustain efforts in combating DBD transmission.

title: Detection of Dengue Virus in Aedes aegypti Eggs Supports Vertical Transmission in Natural Settings
abstract: Dengue remains one of the most important mosquito-borne viral diseases worldwide, and vector control continues to be the cornerstone of disease prevention. Vertical transmission has been proposed as a mechanism contributing to the maintenance of dengue virus (DENV) during interepidemic periods. In this study, field-collected egg pools and second-generation eggs derived from field-collected females from the state of Rio de Janeiro were analyzed by RT-qPCR, Sanger sequencing, plaque assay, and transmission electron microscopy. The second-generation egg samples (E1–E4), corresponding to F2 eggs of the AEDES-RIO strain, were all DENV positive. Sample E1 was positive for DENV-1, whereas samples E2–E4 were positive for DENV-4, confirming transovarial vertical transmission. The detection of DENV-1 and DENV-2 in field-collected egg pools further supports the occurrence of vertical transmission. All PCR-amplified viral fragments were confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Furthermore, homogenized egg samples naturally infected with DENV successfully infected Vero cells, demonstrating that the virus remained infectious. Transmission electron microscopy revealed virus-like particles of approximately 50 nm in diameter within egg tissues, providing ultrastructural evidence that corroborated the molecular and virological findings. Collectively, these findings provide additional evidence supporting vertical transmission of DENV in naturally infected Aedes aegypti populations and highlight the potential of egg-based surveillance as a complementary tool for entomological monitoring. However, further longitudinal studies are needed to establish its epidemiological value.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue remains a major mosquito-borne viral disease globally, and vector control is the primary prevention strategy, yet gaps persist in understanding how the virus persists during interepidemic periods. The study aimed to investigate whether vertical transmission in Aedes aegypti could contribute to dengue virus maintenance in natural settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Field-collected egg pools and second-generation eggs from Aedes aegypti females in Rio de Janeiro were analyzed to detect dengue virus (DENV) and assess vertical transmission. Samples included field-collected egg pools and F2 generation eggs derived from field-collected females.
analysis.methods: RT-qPCR, Sanger sequencing, plaque assay, and transmission electron microscopy were used to detect and characterize DENV in egg samples. PCR-amplified viral fragments were confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and homogenized egg samples were tested for infectivity in Vero cells.
analysis.main_results: All second-generation egg samples (E1–E4) were DENV positive, with E1 positive for DENV-1 and E2–E4 positive for DENV-4, confirming transovarial vertical transmission. Virus-like particles of approximately 50 nm were observed in egg tissues by transmission electron microscopy, and homogenized egg samples infected Vero cells, demonstrating retained infectivity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The detection of DENV-1 and DENV-2 in field-collected egg pools further supports vertical transmission in natural Aedes aegypti populations. This study provides direct evidence of vertical transmission in field settings, highlighting a potential mechanism for DENV maintenance between epidemics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that egg-based surveillance could complement entomological monitoring for dengue control programs. Vertical transmission may contribute to DENV persistence, informing surveillance and control strategies during interepidemic periods.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and reliance on field-collected samples, which may not capture temporal dynamics or population-wide trends. Additional longitudinal studies are needed to establish the epidemiological significance of vertical transmission in natural settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated vertical transmission of dengue virus (DENV) in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, addressing a key gap in understanding DENV persistence during interepidemic periods. Field-collected egg pools and second-generation eggs were analyzed using RT-qPCR, Sanger sequencing, plaque assay, and transmission electron microscopy. All second-generation egg samples were DENV positive, with DENV-1 detected in one sample and DENV-4 in three others, confirming transovarial vertical transmission. Virus-like particles (~50 nm) were observed in egg tissues, and homogenized egg samples infected Vero cells, demonstrating retained infectivity. The detection of DENV-1 and DENV-2 in field-collected egg pools further supported vertical transmission in natural settings. These findings suggest egg-based surveillance could enhance entomological monitoring, though longitudinal studies are needed to assess epidemiological value.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热仍然是全球主要的蚊媒病毒性疾病,媒介 控制是主要预防策略,但对于该病毒在流行期间如何持续存在的了解仍然存在差距。该研究旨在调查埃及伊蚊的垂直 传播 是否有助于自然环境中 登革病毒 的维持。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对里约热内卢现场采集的卵池和雌性埃及伊蚊的第二代卵进行分析,以检测 登革病毒 (DENV) 并评估垂直 传播。样本包括现场收集的卵池和来自现场收集的雌性的 F2 代卵。
elements_zh.methods: RT-qPCR、Sanger 测序、噬菌斑测定和 传播 电子显微镜用于检测和表征鸡蛋样品中的 DENV。PCR 扩增的病毒片段通过桑格测序进行确认,并测试匀浆鸡蛋样本在 Vero 细胞中的感染性。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有第二代卵子样本(E1-E4)均为DENV阳性,其中E1为DENV-1阳性,E2-E4为DENV-4阳性,证实了经卵巢垂直传播。通过传播电子显微镜在鸡蛋组织中观察到约50 nm的病毒样颗粒,并且匀浆的鸡蛋样品感染了Vero细胞,证明了保留的感染性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在现场收集的卵池中检测到 DENV-1 和 DENV-2 进一步支持了自然埃及伊蚊种群中的垂直 传播。这项研究提供了现场环境中垂直 传播 的直接证据,强调了流行病之间 DENV 维持的潜在机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,基于鸡蛋的 监测 可以补充登革热控制计划的昆虫学监测。垂直监测可能有助于DENV持续存在,为监测和流行期间的控制策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其横截面设计和对现场采集样本的依赖而受到限制,这些样本可能无法捕捉时间动态或人群范围内的趋势。需要进行额外的纵向研究来确定自然环境中垂直 传播 的流行病学意义。

source_body_en: Dengue remains one of the most important mosquito-borne viral diseases worldwide, and vector control continues to be the cornerstone of disease prevention. Vertical transmission has been proposed as a mechanism contributing to the maintenance of dengue virus (DENV) during interepidemic periods. In this study, field-collected egg pools and second-generation eggs derived from field-collected females from the state of Rio de Janeiro were analyzed by RT-qPCR, Sanger sequencing, plaque assay, and transmission electron microscopy. The second-generation egg samples (E1–E4), corresponding to F2 eggs of the AEDES-RIO strain, were all DENV positive. Sample E1 was positive for DENV-1, whereas samples E2–E4 were positive for DENV-4, confirming transovarial vertical transmission. The detection of DENV-1 and DENV-2 in field-collected egg pools further supports the occurrence of vertical transmission. All PCR-amplified viral fragments were confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Furthermore, homogenized egg samples naturally infected with DENV successfully infected Vero cells, demonstrating that the virus remained infectious. Transmission electron microscopy revealed virus-like particles of approximately 50 nm in diameter within egg tissues, providing ultrastructural evidence that corroborated the molecular and virological findings. Collectively, these findings provide additional evidence supporting vertical transmission of DENV in naturally infected Aedes aegypti populations and highlight the potential of egg-based surveillance as a complementary tool for entomological monitoring. However, further longitudinal studies are needed to establish its epidemiological value.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对里约热内卢现场采集的卵池和雌性埃及伊蚊的第二代卵进行分析,以检测 登革病毒 (DENV) 并评估垂直 传播。样本包括现场收集的卵池和来自现场收集的雌性的 F2 代卵。

analysis_zh.main_results: 所有第二代卵子样本(E1-E4)均为DENV阳性,其中E1为DENV-1阳性,E2-E4为DENV-4阳性,证实了经卵巢垂直传播。通过传播电子显微镜在鸡蛋组织中观察到约50 nm的病毒样颗粒,并且匀浆的鸡蛋样品感染了Vero细胞,证明了保留的感染性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在现场收集的卵池中检测到 DENV-1 和 DENV-2 进一步支持了自然埃及伊蚊种群中的垂直 传播。这项研究提供了现场环境中垂直 传播 的直接证据,强调了流行病之间 DENV 维持的潜在机制。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,基于鸡蛋的 监测 可以补充登革热控制计划的昆虫学监测。垂直监测可能有助于DENV持续存在,为监测和流行期间的控制策略提供信息。

title: A qualitative evaluation of dengue surveillance system implementation in southern Iran following autochthonous transmission
abstract: Dengue fever, a re-emerging mosquito-borne viral disease, poses an escalating global health threat exacerbated by climate change and globalization. While Iran has historically reported only imported dengue cases, autochthonous transmission has been documented in southern provinces, particularly Hormozgan, following the first confirmed local transmission in 2024. Understanding stakeholders’ perspectives on the implementation of the national dengue surveillance system is therefore critical for informing evidence-based preparedness and policy-making. This retrospective qualitative study was conducted in Hormozgan Province between February and March 2025. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using directed content analysis guided by the CDC surveillance evaluation framework. Key surveillance attributes—including simplicity, data quality, acceptability, sensitivity, representativeness, and timeliness—were used as analytical categories to interpret participants’ perceptions of system performance. Nineteen participants—including senior and mid-level managers, public health experts, and provincial officials—were recruited through purposive sampling with maximum variation until data saturation was achieved. Data were analyzed using MAXQDA 2020, and trustworthiness was ensured based on Lincoln and Guba’s criteria. Five major themes emerged: (1) Simplicity of processes and system adaptability, (2) Data quality, integration, and acceptability challenges, (3) Early detection, clinical recognition, and diagnostic workflow limitations, (4) Comprehensive population coverage and rapid response, and (5) System sustainability and data utilization challenges. Participants identified reference laboratories and successful local initiatives as important strengths, alongside challenges such as parallel reporting systems, limited private-sector engagement, perceived false-negative rapid diagnostic test results during early-stage illness, incomplete migrant population coverage, and unstable digital infrastructure. The findings suggest that dengue surveillance in Iran is transitioning from a focus on imported cases to the management of local transmission. Participants highlighted challenges related to data integration, intersectoral coordination, and the coverage of vulnerable populations despite existing surveillance capacities. Strengthening surveillance integration, digital reporting systems, early diagnostic capacity, and cross-sector collaboration may improve timeliness, coverage, and overall preparedness.

title_zh: 继本土 监测 系统实施后,对伊朗南部登革热 监测 系统实施的定性评估
source_body_en: Dengue fever, a re-emerging mosquito-borne viral disease, poses an escalating global health threat exacerbated by climate change and globalization. While Iran has historically reported only imported dengue cases, autochthonous transmission has been documented in southern provinces, particularly Hormozgan, following the first confirmed local transmission in 2024. Understanding stakeholders’ perspectives on the implementation of the national dengue surveillance system is therefore critical for informing evidence-based preparedness and policy-making. This retrospective qualitative study was conducted in Hormozgan Province between February and March 2025. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using directed content analysis guided by the CDC surveillance evaluation framework. Key surveillance attributes—including simplicity, data quality, acceptability, sensitivity, representativeness, and timeliness—were used as analytical categories to interpret participants’ perceptions of system performance. Nineteen participants—including senior and mid-level managers, public health experts, and provincial officials—were recruited through purposive sampling with maximum variation until data saturation was achieved. Data were analyzed using MAXQDA 2020, and trustworthiness was ensured based on Lincoln and Guba’s criteria. Five major themes emerged: (1) Simplicity of processes and system adaptability, (2) Data quality, integration, and acceptability challenges, (3) Early detection, clinical recognition, and diagnostic workflow limitations, (4) Comprehensive population coverage and rapid response, and (5) System sustainability and data utilization challenges. Participants identified reference laboratories and successful local initiatives as important strengths, alongside challenges such as parallel reporting systems, limited private-sector engagement, perceived false-negative rapid diagnostic test results during early-stage illness, incomplete migrant population coverage, and unstable digital infrastructure. The findings suggest that dengue surveillance in Iran is transitioning from a focus on imported cases to the management of local transmission. Participants highlighted challenges related to data integration, intersectoral coordination, and the coverage of vulnerable populations despite existing surveillance capacities. Strengthening surveillance integration, digital reporting systems, early diagnostic capacity, and cross-sector collaboration may improve timeliness, coverage, and overall preparedness.

title: Analysis of Dengue-Related Deaths in Colombia During the 2024 Outbreak
abstract: Background: Dengue is a viral disease transmitted by vectors, mainly by Aedes mosquitoes. Objective: To analyze dengue-related deaths in Colombia during the 2024 outbreak. Methodology: An observational, descriptive, and retrospective study. Secondary sources provided by Instituto Nacional de Salud de Colombia, were used. Absolute and relative frequencies with 95% confidence intervals were calculated for categorical variables, and measures of central tendency and dispersion were computed for quantitative variables. Results: In 2024, 284 confirmed dengue-related deaths were recorded in Colombia, with a higher predominance in females during the adult stage; the department with the highest number of deaths was Valle del Cauca. The departments of Guainía (0.35), La Guajira, and Putumayo (0.26) showing the highest case fatality rates. Differences were identified among age groups: individuals aged 50 to 59 years showed the greatest delay in seeking care, with an average of 4.93 days (SD: 1.73), while children aged 1 to 4 years sought care more promptly, with an average of 2.9 days (SD: 2.5). Additionally, children under 1 year of age had the shortest mean interval between hospitalization and death, with only 1.8 days (SD: 0.7) . Conclusion: These findings highlight the need to strengthen surveillance actions, timely diagnosis, and the problem-solving capacity of health services, especially in vulnerable contexts and during periods of higher transmission.
journal: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science

source_records.abstract: Background: Dengue is a viral disease transmitted by vectors, mainly by Aedes mosquitoes. Objective: To analyze dengue-related deaths in Colombia during the 2024 outbreak. Methodology: An observational, descriptive, and retrospective study. Secondary sources provided by Instituto Nacional de Salud de Colombia, were used. Absolute and relative frequencies with 95% confidence intervals were calculated for categorical variables, and measures of central tendency and dispersion were computed for quantitative variables. Results: In 2024, 284 confirmed dengue-related deaths were recorded in Colombia, with a higher predominance in females during the adult stage; the department with the highest number of deaths was Valle del Cauca. The departments of Guainía (0.35), La Guajira, and Putumayo (0.26) showing the highest case fatality rates. Differences were identified among age groups: individuals aged 50 to 59 years showed the greatest delay in seeking care, with an average of 4.93 days (SD: 1.73), while children aged 1 to 4 years sought care more promptly, with an average of 2.9 days (SD: 2.5). Additionally, children under 1 year of age had the shortest mean interval between hospitalization and death, with only 1.8 days (SD: 0.7) . Conclusion: These findings highlight the need to strengthen surveillance actions, timely diagnosis, and the problem-solving capacity of health services, especially in vulnerable contexts and during periods of higher transmission.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease of public-health importance in Colombia, yet detailed analyses of fatal outcomes during the 2024 outbreak were lacking. The study aimed to quantify and characterize dengue-related deaths to inform control priorities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An observational, descriptive, and retrospective study was conducted using secondary surveillance data from the Instituto Nacional de Salud de Colombia covering the 2024 dengue outbreak.
analysis.methods: Absolute and relative frequencies with 95% confidence intervals were calculated for categorical variables, and measures of central tendency and dispersion were computed for quantitative variables using national surveillance records.
analysis.main_results: In 2024, 284 confirmed dengue-related deaths were recorded in Colombia, with a higher predominance in females during the adult stage; the department with the highest number of deaths was Valle del Cauca. The departments of Guainía (0.35), La Guajira, and Putumayo (0.26) showed the highest case fatality rates.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the geographic and demographic patterns as evidence that surveillance, timely diagnosis, and health-service capacity must be strengthened, particularly in high-fatality departments and among adults with delayed care-seeking.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can guide targeted surveillance and clinical interventions in departments with elevated case fatality and among adult populations with prolonged pre-hospital delays.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s reliance on secondary surveillance data and its retrospective design limit causal inference and generalizability, warranting a moderate strength of evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective observational study analyzed 284 confirmed dengue-related deaths in Colombia during the 2024 outbreak using national surveillance data. Females in the adult stage predominated among fatalities, and Valle del Cauca reported the highest absolute number of deaths. Case fatality rates were highest in Guainía (0.35), La Guajira, and Putumayo (0.26). Adults aged 50–59 years had the longest delay before seeking care (mean 4.93 days), while children under 1 year had the shortest interval between hospitalization and death (mean 1.8 days). The authors conclude that strengthening surveillance, timely diagnosis, and health-service capacity is critical, especially in high-fatality departments and among vulnerable groups.

title: Association of Dengue Virus Serotypes with Disease Severity and Clinical-Hematological Parameters: A Hospital-Based Analytical Study
abstract: Abstract Background: Dengue disease severity varies by viral serotype and host factors. This study examined associations between dengue virus (DENV) serotypes, disease severity, and clinical-hematological parameters. Aims & Objectives: To investigate the molecular epidemiology of circulating dengue serotypes, identify DENV-1 to DENV-4 by RT-PCR, determine their demographic and clinical distribution, assess associations with disease severity, and generate data to strengthen dengue surveillance and public health interventions. Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 290 clinically suspected dengue patients at Index Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, Indore, from January 2023 to January 2026. Serum samples were screened using the SD BIOLINETM Dengue Duo Rapid Test, followed by viral RNA extraction and real-time RT-PCR with the RealStar® Dengue Type RT-PCR Kit 1.0. Dengue serotypes were identified, and clinical and hematological parameters were compared according to disease severity. Results: Real-time RT-PCR confirmed dengue infection in 67 (23.1%) patients. DENV-2 was the predominant serotype (46.3%), followed by DENV-3 (26.9%), DENV-1 (20.9%), DENV-4 (3.0%), and mixed infections (3.0%). Serotype was significantly associated with disease severity (p=0.012). Mean platelet count declined significantly from 142,800/μL in dengue without warning signs to 42,300/μL in severe dengue (p<0.001). Thrombocytopenia was the most common hematological abnormality (88.1%). DENV-2 infection, platelet count <50,000/μL, bleeding manifestations, and abdominal pain were independently associated with severe dengue. Conclusion: DENV-2 predominated and was significantly associated with severe dengue. Molecular serotyping combined with clinical and hematological assessment may facilitate early identification of patients at risk of severe disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue disease severity varies by viral serotype and host factors, creating a need to clarify how specific dengue virus (DENV) serotypes influence clinical outcomes and hematological parameters to inform surveillance and public health interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A hospital-based cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 290 clinically suspected dengue patients at Index Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, Indore, from January 2023 to January 2026.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were screened using the SD BIOLINETM Dengue Duo Rapid Test, followed by viral RNA extraction and real-time RT-PCR with the RealStar® Dengue Type RT-PCR Kit 1.0 to identify DENV serotypes, and clinical and hematological parameters were compared according to disease severity.
analysis.main_results: Real-time RT-PCR confirmed dengue infection in 67 (23.1%) patients, with DENV-2 predominating (46.3%), followed by DENV-3 (26.9%), DENV-1 (20.9%), DENV-4 (3.0%), and mixed infections (3.0%). Serotype was significantly associated with disease severity (p=0.012), and mean platelet count declined from 142,800/μL in dengue without warning signs to 42,300/μL in severe dengue (p<0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that DENV-2 predominated and was significantly associated with severe dengue, suggesting that molecular serotyping combined with clinical and hematological assessment may facilitate early identification of patients at risk of severe disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform dengue surveillance strategies by prioritizing DENV-2 monitoring and integrating serotype-specific risk stratification into clinical management to improve early detection of severe cases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and hospital-based sampling limit causal inference and generalizability to the broader population, and the evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to potential selection bias and unmeasured confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This hospital-based cross-sectional study in Indore, India, analyzed 290 clinically suspected dengue patients from 2023 to 2026 to investigate associations between dengue virus (DENV) serotypes, disease severity, and clinical-hematological parameters. Using RT-PCR, DENV-2 was identified as the predominant serotype (46.3%), followed by DENV-3 (26.9%), DENV-1 (20.9%), DENV-4 (3.0%), and mixed infections (3.0%). Serotype was significantly associated with disease severity (p=0.012), and severe dengue cases showed marked thrombocytopenia (mean platelet count 42,300/μL). DENV-2 infection, platelet count <50,000/μL, bleeding manifestations, and abdominal pain were independently associated with severe disease. The authors propose that molecular serotyping combined with clinical and hematological assessment could aid early identification of high-risk patients. However, the cross-sectional design and hospital-based sampling limit causal inference and generalizability, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热疾病的严重程度因病毒血清型和 宿主 因素而异,因此需要澄清特定的 登革病毒 (DENV) 血清型如何影响临床结果和血液学参数,以便为 监测 和公共卫生干预措施提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023 年 1 月至 2026 年 1 月,印多尔 Index 医学院医院和研究中心对 290 名临床疑似登革热患者进行了一项以医院为基础的横断面分析研究。

elements_zh.main_results: 实时RT-PCR证实67例(23.1%)患者感染登革热,其中以DENV-2为主(46.3%),其次是DENV-3(26.9%)、DENV-1(20.9%)、DENV-4(3.0%)和混合感染(3.0%)。血清型与疾病严重程度显着相关(p=0.012),平均血小板计数从无警告信号的登革热中的 142,800/μL 下降至 重症登革热 中的 42,300/μL(p<0.001)。

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that DENV-2 predominated and was significantly associated with severe dengue, suggesting that molecular serotyping combined with clinical and hematological assessment may facilitate early identification of patients at risk of severe disease.

title_zh: 登革病毒 血清型与疾病严重程度和临床血液学参数的关联:基于医院的分析研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background: Dengue disease severity varies by viral serotype and host factors. This study examined associations between dengue virus (DENV) serotypes, disease severity, and clinical-hematological parameters. Aims & Objectives: To investigate the molecular epidemiology of circulating dengue serotypes, identify DENV-1 to DENV-4 by RT-PCR, determine their demographic and clinical distribution, assess associations with disease severity, and generate data to strengthen dengue surveillance and public health interventions. Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 290 clinically suspected dengue patients at Index Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, Indore, from January 2023 to January 2026. Serum samples were screened using the SD BIOLINETM Dengue Duo Rapid Test, followed by viral RNA extraction and real-time RT-PCR with the RealStar® Dengue Type RT-PCR Kit 1.0. Dengue serotypes were identified, and clinical and hematological parameters were compared according to disease severity. Results: Real-time RT-PCR confirmed dengue infection in 67 (23.1%) patients. DENV-2 was the predominant serotype (46.3%), followed by DENV-3 (26.9%), DENV-1 (20.9%), DENV-4 (3.0%), and mixed infections (3.0%). Serotype was significantly associated with disease severity (p=0.012). Mean platelet count declined significantly from 142,800/μL in dengue without warning signs to 42,300/μL in severe dengue (p<0.001). Thrombocytopenia was the most common hematological abnormality (88.1%). DENV-2 infection, platelet count <50,000/μL, bleeding manifestations, and abdominal pain were independently associated with severe dengue. Conclusion: DENV-2 predominated and was significantly associated with severe dengue. Molecular serotyping combined with clinical and hematological assessment may facilitate early identification of patients at risk of severe disease.
