title: Efektivitas Kompres Hangat dan Tepid Water Sponge pada Anak dengan Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever: Studi Kasus
abstract: Pendahuluan: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) merupakan penyakit infeksi yang banyak menyerang anak dan ditandai dengan demam tinggi. Selain terapi farmakologis, intervensi non-farmakologis seperti kompres hangat dan teknik tepid sponge sering digunakan, namun bukti perbandingan efektivitas keduanya masih terbatas. Tujuan: Tujuan studi kasus ini adalah untuk mengetahui perbedaan efektivitas kompres hangat konvensional dan teknik tepid sponge dalam menurunkan suhu tubuh pada anak dengan DHF. Metode: Desain studi kasus deskriptif komparatif pada dua pasien anak dengan DHF yang di ruang rawat inap RS Indriati Solo Baru. Masing-masing pasien diberikan intervensi berbeda selama tiga hari. Pengukuran suhu tubuh dilakukan sebelum dan sesudah intervensi menggunakan termometer digital, serta respon subjektif dan objektif dicatat melalui lembar observasi. Analisis data dilakukan secara deskriptif dengan membandingkan perubahan suhu tubuh antar intervensi. Hasil: Kedua intervensi terbukti efektif menurunkan suhu tubuh. Pada pasien dengan kompres hangat, suhu menurun dari 38,9°C menjadi 37,2°C dengan rata-rata penurunan 0,87°C. Pada pasien dengan tepid sponge, suhu menurun dari 39,7°C menjadi 37,4°C dengan rata-rata penurunan 1,20°C. Respon klinis menunjukkan perbaikan kondisi, termasuk penurunan nadi dan peningkatan aktivitas. Simpulan: Teknik tepid sponge lebih efektif dalam menurunkan suhu tubuh dibandingkan kompres hangat, meskipun kompres hangat lebih nyaman bagi pasien anak.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) merupakan penyakit infeksi yang banyak menyerang anak dan ditandai dengan demam tinggi. Studi ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui perbedaan efektivitas kompres hangat konvensional dan teknik tepid sponge dalam menurunkan suhu tubuh pada anak dengan DHF.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Studi kasus ini menggunakan desain deskriptif komparatif pada dua pasien anak dengan DHF yang dirawat di ruang rawat inap RS Indriati Solo Baru. Masing-masing pasien diberikan intervensi berbeda selama tiga hari.
analysis.methods: Pengukuran suhu tubuh dilakukan sebelum dan sesudah intervensi menggunakan termometer digital, serta respon subjektif dan objektif dicatat melalui lembar observasi. Analisis data dilakukan secara deskriptif dengan membandingkan perubahan suhu tubuh antar intervensi.
analysis.main_results: Kedua intervensi terbukti efektif menurunkan suhu tubuh. Pada pasien dengan kompres hangat, suhu menurun dari 38,9°C menjadi 37,2°C dengan rata-rata penurunan 0,87°C. Pada pasien dengan tepid sponge, suhu menurun dari 39,7°C menjadi 37,4°C dengan rata-rata penurunan 1,20°C.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Teknik tepid sponge lebih efektif dalam menurunkan suhu tubuh dibandingkan kompres hangat, meskipun kompres hangat lebih nyaman bagi pasien anak.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of warm compress and tepid sponge techniques in reducing body temperature in children with Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF). It was a descriptive comparative case study conducted on two patients at RS Indriati Solo Baru. Each patient received a different intervention over three days, with body temperature measured before and after using a digital thermometer. Subjective and objective responses were recorded via an observation sheet. Both interventions were found effective, with tepid sponge showing a greater reduction in temperature (from 39.7°C to 37.4°C, average decrease of 1.20°C) compared to warm compress (from 38.9°C to 37.2°C, average decrease of 0.87°C). The authors concluded that tepid sponge is more effective in lowering body temperature in children with DHF, although warm compress is more comfortable. The study's small sample size and lack of formal statistical analysis limit the strength of the evidence, but the findings provide practical insights for clinical management of DHF in pediatric patients.

title: Intrauterine exposure to the dengue virus and the neurodevelopment of offspring
abstract: Dengue is the most widespread and rapidly growing vector-borne infectious disease. It is estimated 2.5 billion people across 129 countries live in tropical and subtropical regions where the disease is endemic and are at risk of contracting dengue. An estimated 105 million people are infected worldwide each year. Many studies have reported associations between exposure to dengue virus infection and gestational complications. Similarly, there is evidence linking dengue to impaired placental blood flow and compromised fetal development, including the formation of fetal nervous system structures. Furthermore, it has been proposed that infection-related Maternal Immune Activation (MIA) increases the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders. Thus, this study is justified by the need to gather and compile data on the impact of dengue during pregnancy on offspring neurodevelopment, providing scientific evidence to inform the care of children exposed to DENV in utero. The objective is to map the evidence in the literature regarding intrauterine exposure to DENV and structural and functional neurodevelopmental outcomes in the offspring. Given the context presented, children exposed to DENV during gestation are expected to be at higher risk of neurodevelopmental delays compared to unexposed children.

title: Strain-Specific Reduction of Ndel1 Enzymatic Activity During Early Zika Virus Infection in the Neonatal Brain
abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection during early development is associated with severe neurodevelopmental impairment, including congenital microcephaly, yet the molecular mechanisms linking viral exposure to neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Ndel1 (nudE neurodevelopment protein 1 like 1) is an oligopeptidase critically involved in neuronal migration, neurite outgrowth, and cytoskeletal dynamics, processes essential for proper brain development. Building on previous observations that Ndel1 enzymatic activity is reduced in ZIKV-infected embryonic and neonatal brains, we investigated whether this modulation represents a conserved host response or a strain-specific molecular effect. Using a neonatal intracerebroventricular infection model in Swiss mice at postnatal day 0, we compared the effects of a Brazilian ZIKV strain (ZIKV BR ), an African lineage strain (ZIKV AF ), and dengue virus (DENV) on Ndel1 regulation in the brain. We found that Ndel1 enzymatic activity was significantly reduced at early post-infection time points (P3 and P7) exclusively in ZIKV BR -infected animals, whereas ZIKV AF and DENV did not alter enzyme activity relative to controls. Notably, at the earliest timepoint (P3), this reduction occurred in the absence of changes in Ndel1 mRNA expression, indicating an initial post-transcriptional or functional mechanism of regulation, although Ndel1 mRNA expression was also significantly reduced by P7. Although both ZIKV strains induced robust inflammatory gene expression, only ZIKV BR infection resulted in decreased Ndel1 activity, dissociating neuroinflammatory signaling from enzymatic modulation. Importantly, this strain-specific reduction parallels the unique capacity of ZIKV BR to induce microcephaly and supports Ndel1 dysfunction as an early molecular event associated with neurodevelopmental impairment. Together, these findings identify a virus- and strain-specific regulation of a key neuronal enzyme and provide mechanistic insight into the molecular basis of ZIKV BR -associated neurodevelopmental outcomes.

Building on previous observations that Ndel1 enzymatic activity is reduced in ZIKV-infected embryonic and neonatal brains, we investigated whether this modulation represents a conserved host response or a strain-specific molecular effect. Using a neonatal intracerebroventricular infection model in Swiss mice at postnatal day 0, we compared the effects of a Brazilian ZIKV strain (ZIKV BR ), an African lineage strain (ZIKV AF ), and dengue virus (DENV) on Ndel1 regulation in the brain. We found that Ndel1 enzymatic activity was significantly reduced at early post-infection time points (P3 and P7) exclusively in ZIKV BR -infected animals, whereas ZIKV AF and DENV did not alter enzyme activity relative to controls. Notably, at the earliest timepoint (P3), this reduction occurred in the absence of changes in Ndel1 mRNA expression, indicating an initial post-transcriptional or functional mechanism of regulation, although Ndel1 mRNA expression was also significantly reduced by P7. Although both ZIKV strains induced robust inflammatory gene expression, only ZIKV BR infection resulted in decreased Ndel1 activity, dissociating neuroinflammatory signaling from enzymatic modulation. Importantly, this strain-specific reduction parallels the unique capacity of ZIKV BR to induce microcephaly and supports Ndel1 dysfunction as an early molecular event associated with neurodevelopmental impairment. Together, these findings identify a virus- and strain-specific regulation of a key neuronal enzyme and provide mechanistic insight into the molecular basis of ZIKV BR -associated neurodevelopmental outcomes.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖新生小鼠模型而受到限制,该模型可能无法完全重现人类神经发育过程。由于缺乏人类数据并且关注感染后早期时间点,证据强度中等。

title: A dengue sob uma perspectiva epidemiológica e sociodemográfica: uma análise sobre o estado de Minas Gerais
abstract: O contexto epidemiológico da dengue no Brasil caracteriza-se por oscilações entre períodos endêmicos e surtos epidêmicos, representando um desafio contínuo à saúde pública. Este estudo tem como objetivo geral analisar o perfil epidemiológico e sociodemográfico da dengue no estado de Minas Gerais, com ênfase no município de Uberlândia, a partir de evidências da literatura científica recente. Trata-se de uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de caráter descritivo e exploratório, realizada em bases de dados nacionais e internacionais. Os resultados indicam elevada incidência da doença em determinados períodos do ano, forte associação com fatores socioambientais, desigualdades regionais e impacto significativo sobre o Sistema Único de Saúde. title: Liver Organoids: From Disease Modelling to Regenerative Medicine
abstract: ABSTRACT Liver organoids are three‐dimensional miniature liver models that recapitulate the complex architecture and key functions of the human liver in vitro, offering powerful platforms for both fundamental research and translational applications. This review systematically summarises current fabrication strategies, disease‐modelling utilities and regenerative potentials of liver organoids, alongside the major challenges and future directions. In recent years, the field has witnessed several breakthroughs. Through endothelial co‐culture approaches, vascularised and metabolically zonated liver organoids have been successfully generated, achieving endothelial coverage exceeding 85%. Prime editing enables precise correction of pathogenic mutations in patient‐derived organoids, with no off‐target effects detected at the genome‐wide level. In disease modelling, iPSC‐derived liver organoids faithfully recapitulate the pathological progression of metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and verify the lipid‐lowering efficacy of semaglutide. Macrophage‐integrated organoid models support the full life cycles of HEV, SARS‐CoV‐2 and dengue virus, providing new tools for antiviral drug screening. Large‐scale patient‐derived tumour organoid biobanks successfully preserve the heterogeneity and clinical drug‐resistance signatures of liver cancers. In regenerative medicine, encapsulated hepatocyte organoids and the UTOpiA bioartificial liver system have effectively rescued acute liver failure in animal models, while gene‐edited autologous organoids offer potential curative strategies for genetic disorders such as Wilson disease. Nevertheless, insufficient hepatocyte functional maturity, difficulties in constructing vascular networks, and the lack of standardised culture protocols remain major obstacles to clinical translation. By bridging fundamental liver biology and clinical practice, liver organoid technology lays a solid foundation for precision hepatology and regenerative therapies. Continued interdisciplinary efforts are still required to overcome current limitations and facilitate its clinical adoption.

analysis.scope_and_question: The scope examines liver organoids as in vitro models for human liver biology and translational applications, with a central question on their utility in disease modelling and regenerative medicine. The topic boundary excludes non-liver systems and non-organoid platforms.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis summarising fabrication strategies, disease-modelling utilities, and regenerative potentials of liver organoids. It reports breakthroughs such as endothelial co-culture achieving >85% endothelial coverage and prime editing with no off-target effects, but does not provide databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or included-study counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Major areas of agreement include the successful generation of vascularised and metabolically zonated liver organoids through endothelial co-culture, precise correction of pathogenic mutations in patient-derived organoids using prime editing, and the recapitulation of MASLD pathology with verification of semaglutide efficacy in iPSC-derived liver organoids.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Key unresolved challenges include insufficient hepatocyte functional maturity, difficulties in constructing vascular networks, and the lack of standardised culture protocols, which hinder clinical translation. Additionally, while macrophage-integrated organoid models support the full life cycles of certain viruses, their relevance to dengue virus remains unaddressed.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Specific priorities include advancing hepatocyte functional maturity, standardising culture protocols, and developing vascularised organoid systems for clinical applications. The review also highlights the need for interdisciplinary efforts to overcome current limitations and facilitate clinical adoption of liver organoid technology.

analysis.summary_en: Liver organoids are three-dimensional in vitro models that replicate human liver architecture and functions, serving as platforms for disease modelling and regenerative medicine. The review synthesises breakthroughs such as endothelial co-culture achieving >85% endothelial coverage and prime editing with no off-target effects, enabling precise correction of pathogenic mutations in patient-derived organoids. iPSC-derived liver organoids faithfully model MASLD and validate semaglutide efficacy. However, challenges persist, including insufficient hepatocyte maturity, vascular network construction difficulties, and lack of standardised protocols, which impede clinical translation. The review underscores the need for interdisciplinary efforts to address these gaps and advance precision hepatology and regenerative therapies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该范围研究了肝脏类器官作为人类肝脏生物学和转化应用的体外模型,其核心问题是它们在疾病建模和再生医学中的效用。主题边界不包括非肝脏系统和非类器官平台。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是一篇叙述性综合文章,总结了肝脏类器官的制造策略、疾病建模实用程序和再生潜力。它报告了一些突破,例如内皮共培养实现了 >85% 的内皮覆盖率和没有脱靶效应的初等编辑,但没有提供数据库、搜索日期、资格标准或纳入研究计数。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 达成一致的主要领域包括通过内皮共培养成功生成血管化和代谢分区的肝脏类器官,使用prime编辑精确校正患者来源的类器官中的致病性突变,以及重演MASLD病理学并验证索马鲁肽在iPSC来源的肝脏类器官中的功效。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 尚未解决的主要挑战包括肝细胞功能成熟度不足、血管网络构建困难以及缺乏标准化培养方案,这些都阻碍了临床转化。此外,虽然巨噬细胞整合的类器官模型支持某些病毒的整个生命周期,但它们与 登革病毒 的相关性仍未得到解决。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 具体优先事项包括促进肝细胞功能成熟、标准化培养方案以及开发用于临床应用的血管化类器官系统。该审查还强调需要跨学科努力来克服当前的局限性并促进肝脏类器官技术的临床采用。

abstract_zh: 摘要 肝脏类器官是三维微型肝脏模型,在体外概括了人类肝脏的复杂结构和关键功能,为基础研究和转化应用提供了强大的平台。这篇综述系统地总结了肝脏类器官当前的制造策略、疾病建模实用性和再生潜力,以及主要挑战和未来方向。近年来,该领域取得了多项突破。通过内皮共培养方法,已成功生成血管化和代谢分区的肝脏类器官,内皮覆盖率超过 85%。Prime 编辑能够精确校正患者来源的类器官中的致病性 突变,并且在 基因组 范围内未检测到脱靶效应。在疾病建模中,iPSC 衍生的肝脏类器官忠实地再现了代谢功能障碍相关脂肪肝病 (MASLD) 的病理进展,并验证了索马鲁肽的降脂功效。巨噬细胞整合类器官模型支持 HEV、SARS-CoV-2 和 登革病毒 的整个生命周期,为 抗病毒药物 药物筛选提供新工具。大规模患者来源的肿瘤类器官生物库成功保留了肝癌的异质性和临床耐药特征。在再生医学中,封装的肝细胞类器官和 UTOpiA 生物人工肝系统已有效挽救动物模型中的急性肝功能衰竭,而基因编辑的自体类器官则为威尔逊病等遗传性疾病提供了潜在的治疗策略。然而,肝细胞功能成熟度不足、血管网络构建困难以及缺乏标准化培养方案仍然是临床转化的主要障碍。通过连接基础肝脏生物学和临床实践,肝脏类器官技术为精准肝病学和再生治疗奠定了坚实的基础。仍需要持续的跨学科努力来克服当前的局限性并促进其临床采用。

title: A network-driven antiviral discovery pipeline for emerging RNA viruses: a critical perspective from the Red Mexicana de Desarrollo de Antivirales (RMDA).
abstract: INTRODUCTION: RNA viruses impose a disproportionate burden of emerging and reemerging infectious diseases in Latin America, yet antiviral discovery in the region remains fragmented, target-limited, and frequently disconnected from translational pathways. This perspective discusses the Red Mexicana de Desarrollo de Antivirales (RMDA) as a network-driven model to organize antiviral discovery against clinically relevant RNA viruses. AREAS COVERED: The authors describe the conceptual architecture of RMDA, a multi-institutional Mexican initiative that integrates computational prioritization, cell-based antiviral evaluation under BSL-2/BSL-3 conditions, mechanistic virology, assessment of pharmacological synergy, in vivo validation, and clinical linkage through healthcare systems such as the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social. The framework is supported by prior work from participating groups on host-directed and virus-directed candidates, including metabolic modulators, lipid-lowering agents, nuclear transport inhibitors, natural products, polyphenols, melatonin, and rational drug combinations evaluated against dengue virus, Zika virus, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus, and related RNA viruses. EXPERT OPINION: RMDA provides a scalable and regionally adaptable model for antiviral drug discovery in low- and middle-income settings. By aligning distributed expertise, standardized workflows, and translational decision points, this framework may accelerate candidate prioritization, reduce duplication, and strengthen preparedness against RNA virus threats in Mexico and Latin America.

analysis.scope_and_question: The article focuses on dengue virus as a representative emerging RNA pathogen in Latin America, addressing the fragmented and target‐limited antiviral discovery landscape and asking how a network‐driven model (RMDA) can coordinate computational prioritization, in‐vitro testing, mechanistic studies, and clinical linkage to improve antiviral development for dengue and related viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The supplied evidence indicates that the document is a perspective article rather than a systematic review; no databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or formal study selection procedures are reported. The authors describe RMDA as a conceptual framework without detailing a systematic evidence‐gathering methodology.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The authors agree that RMDA constitutes a scalable, regionally adaptable platform that integrates computational screening, BSL‐2/3 cell‐based assays, mechanistic virology, synergy assessment, in‐vivo validation, and clinical linkage, and that this model can strengthen antiviral discovery capacity in low‐ and middle‐income settings.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The abstract provides no empirical outcomes for dengue‐specific candidates, nor does it discuss conflicting data or methodological limitations, leaving a gap in demonstrated efficacy of the RMDA pipeline for dengue virus and in comparative performance versus other antiviral approaches.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: By aligning distributed expertise, standardizing workflows, and defining translational decision points, the RMDA framework may accelerate candidate prioritization, reduce duplication of effort, and enhance preparedness against dengue and other RNA virus threats in Mexico and Latin America.

analysis.summary_en: This perspective examines dengue virus as a key emerging RNA pathogen in Latin America and proposes the Red Mexicana de Desarrollo de Antivirales (RMDA) network‐driven model to overcome fragmented antiviral discovery. The authors describe RMDA’s integrated workflow—from computational prioritization to clinical linkage—and argue it offers a scalable, adaptable solution for low‐ and middle‐income settings. While the article outlines the conceptual architecture and expert endorsement, it lacks reported efficacy data for dengue‐specific candidates, highlighting an evidence gap. The authors suggest that coordinated expertise and standardized pipelines could speed candidate selection, minimize redundancy, and bolster regional preparedness against dengue and other RNA viruses.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The article focuses on dengue virus as a representative emerging RNA pathogen in Latin America, addressing the fragmented and target‐limited antiviral discovery landscape and asking how a network‐driven model (RMDA) can coordinate computational prioritization, in‐vitro testing, mechanistic studies, and clinical linkage to improve antiviral development for dengue and related viruses.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The supplied evidence indicates that the document is a perspective article rather than a systematic review; no databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or formal study selection procedures are reported. analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The authors agree that RMDA constitutes a scalable, regionally adaptable platform that integrates computational screening, BSL‐2/3 cell‐based assays, mechanistic virology, synergy assessment, in‐vivo validation, and clinical linkage, and that this model can strengthen antiviral discovery capacity in low‐ and middle‐income settings.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The abstract provides no empirical outcomes for dengue‐specific candidates, nor does it discuss conflicting data or methodological limitations, leaving a gap in demonstrated efficacy of the RMDA pipeline for dengue virus and in comparative performance versus other antiviral approaches.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: By aligning distributed expertise, standardizing workflows, and defining translational decision points, the RMDA framework may accelerate candidate prioritization, reduce duplication of effort, and enhance preparedness against dengue and other RNA virus threats in Mexico and Latin America.

title_zh: 针对新兴 RNA 病毒的网络驱动的 抗病毒药物 发现管道:来自 Red Mexicana de Desarrollo de 抗病毒药物 (RMDA) 的关键视角。
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: RNA viruses impose a disproportionate burden of emerging and reemerging infectious diseases in Latin America, yet antiviral discovery in the region remains fragmented, target-limited, and frequently disconnected from translational pathways. This perspective discusses the Red Mexicana de Desarrollo de Antivirales (RMDA) as a network-driven model to organize antiviral discovery against clinically relevant RNA viruses. AREAS COVERED: The authors describe the conceptual architecture of RMDA, a multi-institutional Mexican initiative that integrates computational prioritization, cell-based antiviral evaluation under BSL-2/BSL-3 conditions, mechanistic virology, assessment of pharmacological synergy, in vivo validation, and clinical linkage through healthcare systems such as the Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social. The framework is supported by prior work from participating groups on host-directed and virus-directed candidates, including metabolic modulators, lipid-lowering agents, nuclear transport inhibitors, natural products, polyphenols, melatonin, and rational drug combinations evaluated against dengue virus, Zika virus, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus, and related RNA viruses. EXPERT OPINION: RMDA provides a scalable and regionally adaptable model for antiviral drug discovery in low- and middle-income settings. By aligning distributed expertise, standardized workflows, and translational decision points, this framework may accelerate candidate prioritization, reduce duplication, and strengthen preparedness against RNA virus threats in Mexico and Latin America.

title: IFNL1 gene promoter single nucleotide polymorphism rs7247086 enhances transcription through a STAT-binding site.
abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) within the human interferon lambda 1 (IFN-L1, IFN-λ1) gene promoter, rs7247086 (C/T) has been reported to be associated with severe dengue and possibly with psoriasis and COVID-19. However, its functional nature is unknown. The present study was undertaken to examine the effect of rs7247086 on transcription, by utilizing promoter and enhancer-reporter assays. We see that the T allele completes a consensus signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT)-binding site. While we did not find strong evidence to show that the STAT-binding site drove transcription from the IFNL1 gene promoter, we saw that it acts like an enhancer in reporter assays. The T allele of rs7247086 within the STAT-binding site significantly increased transcription of the reporter gene compared to the C allele when incorporated into enhancer-reporter constructs in both HEK293 and A549 cell lines. Mechanistically, we obtained evidence from electrophoretic mobility shift assays to show that the T allele binds to STAT proteins more strongly than the C allele. In a cohort of healthy individuals, we saw that the T allele carriers, specifically males but not females, had significantly increased secretion of IFN-λ1 from their peripheral blood mononuclear cells after stimulation. Lastly, rs7247086 significantly associated with psoriasis, only in males but not in females.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed why the IFNL1 gene promoter SNP rs7247086 (C/T) might influence disease severity in dengue and other conditions, despite its functional role being unknown.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used promoter and enhancer-reporter assays in HEK293 and A549 cell lines to examine the effect of rs7247086 on transcription, alongside electrophoretic mobility shift assays to assess STAT protein binding.
analysis.methods: Promoter and enhancer-reporter constructs incorporating the T or C allele of rs7247086 were tested in HEK293 and A549 cells, and STAT protein binding was evaluated using electrophoretic mobility shift assays.
analysis.main_results: The T allele of rs7247086 significantly increased reporter gene transcription compared to the C allele in both HEK293 and A549 cells, and the T allele showed stronger binding to STAT proteins in electrophoretic mobility shift assays.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the T allele enhances IFNL1 transcription via a STAT-binding site, acting as an enhancer rather than a promoter, and note sex-specific differences in IFN-λ1 secretion and psoriasis association.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that rs7247086 may modulate IFN-λ1 expression, potentially influencing host responses relevant to dengue pathogenesis and other inflammatory conditions, particularly in males.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on in vitro assays and a small cohort, with sex-specific effects observed but not mechanistically explained, warranting cautious interpretation of the evidence strength as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the functional impact of the IFNL1 gene promoter SNP rs7247086 (C/T), previously associated with severe dengue, psoriasis, and COVID-19, but whose functional role was unknown. Using promoter and enhancer-reporter assays in HEK293 and A549 cells, the authors found that the T allele significantly increased reporter gene transcription compared to the C allele. Mechanistically, electrophoretic mobility shift assays showed stronger binding of the T allele to STAT proteins, indicating that the T allele enhances IFNL1 transcription via a STAT-binding site acting as an enhancer. In a small cohort of healthy individuals, male carriers of the T allele exhibited significantly increased IFN-λ1 secretion from peripheral blood mononuclear cells after stimulation, and rs7247086 was significantly associated with psoriasis in males but not females. While these findings suggest a sex-specific modulation of IFN-λ1 expression by rs7247086, the study is limited by its in vitro focus and small sample size, warranting cautious interpretation of the evidence strength.

title: Efficacy of an attractive lethal ovitrap to reduce populations of Aedes mosquitoes: a controlled trial in Iquitos, Peru
abstract: Abstract Introduction Dengue, one of the most important arboviral infections worldwide, is transmitted primarily by the mosquito Aedes aegypti , a vector closely associated with human habitations. Because vector control is the primary prevention strategy for this disease novel tools are urgently needed. We evaluated an Attractive Lethal OviTrap (ALOT) that targets epidemiologically relevant gravid female mosquitoes for public health impact against dengue disease. Methods We conducted a proof-of-concept field efficacy trial in the Amazonian city of Iquitos, Peru, to quantify the reduction of vector density, parity, and sex ratio and symptomatic human dengue infection over a 3.5 year follow-up period. After three baseline entomological surveys in core (753 houses), and buffer (1,549 houses) areas where traps were placed in and around homes, and a control (1,233 houses) area without traps, entomological surveys were carried out every 2 months, and household residents were monitored for dengue disease 3 times a week. Trap maintenance was conducted at 2-3 week intervals by study staff during the first 2.5 years and by residents in the final year. Results Total and female Ae. aegypti abundance demonstrated a strong initial effect with 52% and 47% fewer mosquitoes after trap placement, respectively (Total: RR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.40 – 0.58, p < 0.001; Females: RR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.43 – 0.66, p < 0.001). The effect diminished significantly, however, over the study period (interaction coefficient = 0.035 per month, p < 0.001; interaction coefficient = 0.030 per month, p < 0.001). Female-to-male ratio decreased after trap deployment and impact on non- Aedes abundance was like that of Aedes . Cumulative symptomatic dengue incidence was 1.40% (95% CI: 1.00%-1.70%) in the ALOT area versus 3.20% (95% CI: 2.60%-3.80%) in the control area, a 56% relative reduction (log-rank χ2=30.0, p<0.001). Restricted mean survival time analysis showed participants in the intervention area on average remained dengue-free for 15.5 additional days (95% CI: 11.1-20.0, p<0.001). Conclusions The ALOT strategy functioned as predicted, decreasing but not eliminating female vector densities, with a clear public health impact, lowering dengue disease in areas where traps were deployed. Our study also illustrates the challenges associated with conducting large-scale vector control trials and the need to consider programmatic implementation early in the process of bringing a new product to market. analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue is a major arboviral infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti, necessitating improved vector control tools. The study addressed the urgent need for novel interventions by evaluating whether an Attractive Lethal OviTrap (ALOT) targeting gravid female mosquitoes could reduce vector populations and dengue disease burden.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A proof-of-concept field efficacy trial was conducted in Iquitos, Peru, over 3.5 years. The study included a treatment area with a core (753 houses) and buffer zone (1,549 houses) where ALOT traps were deployed, and a control area (1,233 houses) without traps. Entomological surveys were performed every 2 months, and residents were monitored for symptomatic dengue three times weekly.
analysis.methods: Baseline entomological surveys were conducted prior to trap deployment. Trap maintenance was performed at 2–3 week intervals by staff for the first 2.5 years and by residents in the final year. Mosquito abundance, parity, sex ratio, and human dengue incidence were measured using standardized surveys and active surveillance.
analysis.main_results: Total and female Aedes aegypti abundance decreased by 52% (RR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.40–0.58, p < 0.001) and 47% (RR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.43–0.66, p < 0.001), respectively, after trap placement. The effect diminished over time (interaction coefficient per month: 0.035 and 0.030, p < 0.001). Cumulative symptomatic dengue incidence was 1.40% in the ALOT area versus 3.20% in the control area, a 56% relative reduction (log-rank χ2 = 30.0, p < 0.001), with participants in the intervention area remaining dengue-free for an average of 15.5 additional days (95% CI: 11.1–20.0, p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The ALOT strategy reduced vector densities and dengue incidence as predicted, though it did not eliminate mosquitoes. The trial demonstrated a clear public health impact by lowering dengue disease in treated areas, highlighting the potential of targeted vector control for dengue prevention.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of ALOT traps as a supplementary vector control tool to reduce dengue transmission in endemic urban settings. The study underscores the importance of sustained implementation and programmatic considerations for integrating new vector control tools into public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The effect of the ALOT traps diminished over time, indicating potential challenges with long-term efficacy and user compliance. The evidence is moderate due to the non-randomized design, reliance on community-based maintenance, and the absence of entomological or virological confirmation of dengue infections.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated an Attractive Lethal OviTrap (ALOT) targeting gravid female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in Iquitos, Peru, over 3.5 years. Deployment of ALOT traps in 2,302 houses (core and buffer zones) reduced total and female mosquito abundance by 52% and 47%, respectively, though the effect waned over time. Symptomatic dengue incidence was 56% lower in the intervention area (1.40%) compared to the control area (3.20%), with participants remaining dengue-free for an average of 15.5 additional days. The trial demonstrates that ALOT traps can reduce dengue transmission, but sustained impact requires addressing implementation challenges such as long-term efficacy and community engagement.

title_zh: 有吸引力的致命产卵器减少伊蚊种群的功效:秘鲁伊基托斯的一项对照试验
source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Dengue, one of the most important arboviral infections worldwide, is transmitted primarily by the mosquito Aedes aegypti , a vector closely associated with human habitations. Because vector control is the primary prevention strategy for this disease novel tools are urgently needed. We evaluated an Attractive Lethal OviTrap (ALOT) that targets epidemiologically relevant gravid female mosquitoes for public health impact against dengue disease. Methods We conducted a proof-of-concept field efficacy trial in the Amazonian city of Iquitos, Peru, to quantify the reduction of vector density, parity, and sex ratio and symptomatic human dengue infection over a 3.5 year follow-up period. After three baseline entomological surveys in core (753 houses), and buffer (1,549 houses) areas where traps were placed in and around homes, and a control (1,233 houses) area without traps, entomological surveys were carried out every 2 months, and household residents were monitored for dengue disease 3 times a week. Trap maintenance was conducted at 2-3 week intervals by study staff during the first 2.5 years and by residents in the final year. Results Total and female Ae. aegypti abundance demonstrated a strong initial effect with 52% and 47% fewer mosquitoes after trap placement, respectively (Total: RR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.40 – 0.58, p < 0.001; Females: RR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.43 – 0.66, p < 0.001). The effect diminished significantly, however, over the study period (interaction coefficient = 0.035 per month, p < 0.001; interaction coefficient = 0.030 per month, p < 0.001). Female-to-male ratio decreased after trap deployment and impact on non- Aedes abundance was like that of Aedes . Cumulative symptomatic dengue incidence was 1.40% (95% CI: 1.00%-1.70%) in the ALOT area versus 3.20% (95% CI: 2.60%-3.80%) in the control area, a 56% relative reduction (log-rank χ2=30.0, p<0.001). Restricted mean survival time analysis showed participants in the intervention area on average remained dengue-free for 15.5 additional days (95% CI: 11.1-20.0, p<0.001). Conclusions The ALOT strategy functioned as predicted, decreasing but not eliminating female vector densities, with a clear public health impact, lowering dengue disease in areas where traps were deployed. Our study also illustrates the challenges associated with conducting large-scale vector control trials and the need to consider programmatic implementation early in the process of bringing a new product to market. Author Summary Dengue is one of the most important mosquito transmitted infections worldwide. Aedes aegypti, the most important species involved, has a unique biology living in containers associated with households. New methods to control this mosquito are needed and we present our evaluation of a novel trap called the Attractive Lethal OviTrap (ALOT) that targets older female mosquitoes that are the most important for dengue disease transmission. We conducted a trial in the Amazonian city of Iquitos, Peru, to measure reductions in mosquito numbers, age, and sex ratio and symptomatic human dengue infections over a 3.5 years. After baseline entomological surveys prior to placing ALOT traps in homes in a treatment area, which included a central core area with 753 houses and a protective buffer area with 1,549 houses areas. We also had a control area without any traps in 1,233 houses. Mosquito surveys were carried out every 2 months, and household residents were monitored for dengue disease 3 times per week. The number of all Ae. aegypti were initially reduced by 52% after trap placement whereas females were reduced by 47%. The effect diminished significantly, however, over the study period. Female-to-male ratio decreased after trap deployment and impact on other mosquito species was like that of Aedes . Dengue incidence was 56% less in the area with traps compared to the control area, estimating that participants in the intervention area on average remained dengue-free for 15.5 additional days. The ALOT strategy functioned as predicted, decreasing but not eliminating female mosquitos and had a clear public health impact, lowering dengue disease in areas where traps were deployed.

title: A narrative review of Zika virus cardiotropism and atrial fibrillation from pathogenesis and diagnostic challenges to inflammation aware management
abstract: Systemic inflammation is a key driver of atrial fibrillation (AF), but the mechanisms linking specific viral triggers to arrhythmogenesis are not fully understood. Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, which can induce a significant inflammatory response, provides a compelling clinical model to explore this link. This review synthesizes the current evidence for ZIKV-associated AF, evaluates the proposed pathophysiological mechanisms, and identifies critical knowledge gaps and limitations in the existing literature. Based on preclinical data and clinical case reports, the arrhythmogenic potential of ZIKV appears to be driven by a dual mechanism. Direct viral effects may include cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity and the downregulation of connexin 43 (Cx43), disrupting electrical coupling. Indirectly, a host immune response characterized by elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., TNF-α, IL-6) likely accelerates atrial fibrosis and electrical remodeling, creating a pro-arrhythmic substrate. Diagnosing post-ZIKV AF is challenging due to overlapping symptoms and the arrhythmia’s often paroxysmal nature, necessitating enhanced surveillance with serial ECGs. We propose an “inflammation-aware” management paradigm that considers the virally-induced prothrombotic state when evaluating anticoagulation thresholds and uses advanced imaging like Cardiac MRI to characterize the atrial substrate before interventions such as catheter ablation. While ZIKV serves as an important model for inflammation-driven AF, current evidence remains associative and is derived from limited clinical data. Causality in humans is not yet established. There is an urgent need for methodologically rigorous research, including prospective cohort studies to determine incidence, biomarker validation for risk stratification, and mechanistic studies on human cardiac tissue to confirm the pathways identified in preclinical models and guide the development of targeted therapies.

title: Evaluation of MTego and BG-Sentinel traps for malaria and arbovirus vector surveillance in Cabo Verde.
abstract: Arboviral outbreaks are rising across Africa, a region that continues to face a substantial malaria burden. Cabo Verde remains vulnerable to the emergence and re-emergence of mosquito-borne diseases, including dengue, Zika, and malaria. In January 2024, the World Health Organization certified the country as malaria-free; however, the risk of reintroduction persists. Maintaining malaria-free status requires continuous robust epidemiological and entomological surveillance to prevent local transmission. Innovative vector monitoring and control tools that deliver accurate infestation data are essential in this context. We evaluated the performance of the MTego trap against the BGS traps routinely used in Cabo Verde applying a 4x4 Latin square design with four configurations: 1) BGS with BG Lure; 2) BGS with BG Lure plus CO2; 3) MTego traps with Clay Balls plus PM6 odour bait; and 4) MTego traps with Clay Balls, PM6 bait plus CO2. Sampling was conducted in Praia, before and after the 2023 rainy season. Trap effectiveness was assessed using negative binomial regression models. Across all configurations, 2,673 mosquitoes were collected. Mean nightly catches were highest for BGS traps baited with CO2: 20.4 (95% CI: 15.4-25.4), and lowest for MTego traps: 13.7 (95% CI: 10.0-17.5). Comparative analysis showed that MTego traps outperformed BGS traps in capturing Anopheles arabiensis, with CO2-supplemented MTego trap being the most effective configuration. BGS traps performed best for Aedes aegypti and Culex pipiens sensu lato. Species-specific behavioural patterns were observed, with higher nigh-time catches of Cx pipiens s.l. arabiensis, alongside differences in gonotrophic state. This study highlights the superior performance of MTego traps for malaria surveillance in Cabo Verde.

title_zh: 对佛得角疟疾和虫媒病毒 媒介 监测 的 MTego 和 BG-Sentinel 陷阱进行评估。
source_body_en: Arboviral outbreaks are rising across Africa, a region that continues to face a substantial malaria burden. Cabo Verde remains vulnerable to the emergence and re-emergence of mosquito-borne diseases, including dengue, Zika, and malaria. In January 2024, the World Health Organization certified the country as malaria-free; however, the risk of reintroduction persists. Maintaining malaria-free status requires continuous robust epidemiological and entomological surveillance to prevent local transmission. Innovative vector monitoring and control tools that deliver accurate infestation data are essential in this context. We evaluated the performance of the MTego trap against the BGS traps routinely used in Cabo Verde applying a 4x4 Latin square design with four configurations: 1) BGS with BG Lure; 2) BGS with BG Lure plus CO2; 3) MTego traps with Clay Balls plus PM6 odour bait; and 4) MTego traps with Clay Balls, PM6 bait plus CO2. Sampling was conducted in Praia, before and after the 2023 rainy season. Trap effectiveness was assessed using negative binomial regression models. Across all configurations, 2,673 mosquitoes were collected. Mean nightly catches were highest for BGS traps baited with CO2: 20.4 (95% CI: 15.4-25.4), and lowest for MTego traps: 13.7 (95% CI: 10.0-17.5). Comparative analysis showed that MTego traps outperformed BGS traps in capturing Anopheles arabiensis, with CO2-supplemented MTego trap being the most effective configuration. BGS traps performed best for Aedes aegypti and Culex pipiens sensu lato. Species-specific behavioural patterns were observed, with higher nigh-time catches of Cx pipiens s.l. arabiensis, alongside differences in gonotrophic state. This study highlights the superior performance of MTego traps for malaria surveillance in Cabo Verde.

title: Insecticide susceptibility and knockdown resistance (Kdr) mutations (F1534C and V1016I) in Aedes aegypti populations from Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
abstract: Abstract Background Dengue, Zika and chikungunya are Aedes -borne arboviruses that pose a major global public health threat. In the absence of effective treatments or universally available vaccines, disease control in sub-Saharan Africa relies primarily on insecticidal vector control. However, sustained insecticide application imposes selection pressure for insecticide resistance that compromises intervention effectiveness. This study assessed the insecticide resistance profile of Aedes aegypti populations in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Methods Phenotypic resistance of Ae. aegypti was evaluated using WHO-recommended adulticide and larvicide susceptibility bioassays at 1x discriminating concentrations. F 1 progeny derived from wild Ae. aegypti larvae were used for the tests. In adulticide bioassays, groups of 25 female Ae. aegypti were exposed for 1 h to insecticide-treated WHO susceptibility test papers. Larvicide bioassays exposed 25 third- and fourth-instar larvae to a larvicide based on Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis ( Bti ) or temephos for 24 h in 200 ml of water. Mosquito mortality was recorded 24 h post-exposure. Genotypic resistance was assessed using DNA extracted from phenotyped mosquitoes. The extracted DNA was screened for knockdown resistance ( Kdr ) mutations using diagnostic quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) assays. Results Aedes aegypti populations from Ilala and Temeke districts of Dar es Salaam demonstrated phenotypic resistance to pyrethroids, and organochlorine, with adult mortality rates below 20% and 5%, respectively, while remaining susceptible to organophosphates and carbamates. In Kinondoni, resistance was observed across all classes except carbamates, and pre-exposure to piperonlyl butoxide (PBO) increased pyrethroids mortality to an average of 40%. The LD 50 and LD 90 values for Bti and temephos showed resistance ratios (RR) below 5. The F1534C mutation was detected across all study districts; Ilala (77%, n = 77), Kinondoni (90%, n = 90) and Temeke (83%, n = 83), while low frequencies were observed for V1016I mutation. Conclusion Aedes aegypti populations from Dar es Salaam show widespread resistance to pyrethroids, and organochlorines. There was evidence of metabolic involvement suggested by partial restoration of susceptibility to pyrethroids through pre-exposure to PBO. A two-fold increase in LD90 relative to the susceptible reference strain for Bti and temephos indicates no evidence of resistance, although continued monitoring is warranted to detect potential shifts in susceptibility.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue, Zika and chikungunya are Aedes-borne arboviruses that pose a major global public health threat in sub-Saharan Africa, where disease control relies primarily on insecticidal vector control.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study assessed the insecticide resistance profile of Aedes aegypti populations in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, using F1 progeny derived from wild Ae. aegypti larvae for phenotypic and genotypic resistance testing.
analysis.methods: Phenotypic resistance was evaluated using WHO-recommended adulticide and larvicide susceptibility bioassays at 1x discriminating concentrations, with mosquito mortality recorded 24 hours post-exposure. analysis.main_results: Aedes aegypti populations from Ilala and Temeke districts demonstrated phenotypic resistance to pyrethroids and organochlorines, with adult mortality below 20% and 5%, respectively, while remaining susceptible to organophosphates and carbamates. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the need for integrated vector management strategies in Dar es Salaam, including monitoring resistance trends and evaluating alternative insecticides to sustain vector control effectiveness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to phenotypic and genotypic assessments in three districts of Dar es Salaam, with no data on resistance mechanisms beyond Kdr mutations or broader ecological factors, warranting cautious interpretation and continued surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti populations from Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, using WHO bioassays and qPCR for Kdr mutations. Pyrethroid and organochlorine resistance was widespread, with mortality below 20% and 5% in Ilala and Temeke districts, respectively, while organophosphates and carbamates remained effective. In Kinondoni, resistance extended across most insecticide classes except carbamates, and PBO pre-exposure partially restored pyrethroid susceptibility. The F1534C mutation was highly prevalent (77–90%), whereas V1016I was rare. These results indicate significant operational challenges for vector control in Dar es Salaam, emphasizing the need for resistance monitoring and integrated management strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热、寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅热是伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒,对撒哈拉以南非洲地区的全球公共卫生构成重大威胁,该地区的疾病控制主要依靠杀虫剂 媒介 控制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究利用野生伊蚊的 F1 后代评估了坦桑尼亚达累斯萨拉姆埃及伊蚊种群的杀虫剂抗药性。埃及幼虫用于表型和基因型抗性测试。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 WHO 推荐的杀成虫剂和杀幼虫剂敏感性生物测定法以 1 倍区分浓度评估表型抗性,并在暴露后 24 小时记录蚊子 死亡率。通过使用诊断性 qPCR 检测筛选表型蚊子的 DNA 进行击倒抗性 (Kdr) 突变 来评估基因型抗性。
elements_zh.main_results: 来自伊拉拉和特梅克地区的埃及伊蚊种群表现出对拟除虫菊酯和有机氯的表型抗性,成虫 死亡率 分别低于 20% 和 5%,同时仍然对有机磷酸酯和氨基甲酸酯敏感。在 Kinondoni,除氨基甲酸酯外,所有类别均观察到耐药性,并且预先接触胡椒基丁醚可使拟除虫菊酯 死亡率 平均增加 40%。F1534C 突变 在 Ilala (77%)、Kinondoni (90%) 和 Temeke (83%) 中检测到,而 V1016I 突变 频率较低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究解释了达累斯萨拉姆地区对拟除虫菊酯和有机氯的广泛耐药性。埃及伊蚊种群,PBO 预暴露后拟除虫菊酯敏感性部分恢复表明代谢参与的证据。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了达累斯萨拉姆需要采取综合的 媒介 管理策略,包括监测抗药性趋势和评估替代杀虫剂以维持 媒介 控制有效性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于达累斯萨拉姆三个地区的表型和基因型评估,没有关于 Kdr 监测 或更广泛的生态因素之外的耐药机制的数据,需要谨慎解释和继续 监测。

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 登革热、寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅热是伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒,对全球公共卫生构成重大威胁。在缺乏有效的 治疗 或普遍可用的 疫苗 的情况下,撒哈拉以南非洲地区的疾病控制主要依赖于杀虫剂 媒介 控制。然而,持续使用杀虫剂会给杀虫剂抗药性带来选择压力,从而损害干预效果。本研究评估了坦桑尼亚达累斯萨拉姆埃及伊蚊种群的杀虫剂抗药性。方法 伊蚊表型抗性。使用 WHO 推荐的杀成虫剂和杀幼虫剂敏感性生物测定法以 1 倍区分浓度对埃及伊蚊进行评估。F 1 后代源自野生伊蚊。埃及幼虫用于测试。在杀成虫生物测定中,每组 25 只雌性伊蚊。将埃及伊蚊暴露于经过杀虫剂处理的 WHO 药敏试纸上 1 小时。杀幼虫生物测定将 25 只第三龄和第四龄幼虫暴露于基于以色列苏云金芽孢杆菌 (Bti) 或天美磷的杀幼虫剂(溶于 200 毫升水中)24 小时。暴露后 24 小时记录蚊子 死亡率。使用从表型蚊子中提取的 DNA 评估基因型抗性。使用诊断定量聚合酶链式反应 (qPCR) 分析筛选提取的 DNA 的敲低抗性 (Kdr) 突变。结果 达累斯萨拉姆 Ilala 和 Temeke 区的埃及伊蚊种群表现出对拟除虫菊酯和有机氯的表型抗性,成虫 死亡率 率分别低于 20% 和 5%,同时仍然对有机磷酸酯和氨基甲酸酯敏感。在 Kinondoni,除氨基甲酸酯外,所有类别均观察到耐药性,并且预先暴露于胡椒基丁醚 (PBO) 会使拟除虫菊酯 死亡率 平均增加 40%。Bti 和替美磷的 LD 50 和 LD 90 值显示耐药比 (RR) 低于 5。在所有研究区均检测到 F1534C 突变;Ilala (77%,n = 77)、Kinondoni (90%,n = 90) 和 Temeke (83%,n = 83),而 V1016I 突变 则观察到低频。结论 达累斯萨拉姆的埃及伊蚊种群对拟除虫菊酯和有机氯表现出广泛的抗性。通过预先暴露于 PBO,对拟除虫菊酯的敏感性部分恢复,表明代谢参与的证据。LD90 相对于 Bti 和 temephos 敏感参考菌株增加两倍,表明没有证据表明存在耐药性,尽管需要继续监测以检测敏感性的潜在变化。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热、寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅热是伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒,对撒哈拉以南非洲地区的全球公共卫生构成重大威胁,该地区的疾病控制主要依靠杀虫剂 媒介 控制。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究利用野生伊蚊的 F1 后代评估了坦桑尼亚达累斯萨拉姆埃及伊蚊种群的杀虫剂抗药性。埃及幼虫用于表型和基因型抗性测试。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用 WHO 推荐的杀成虫剂和杀幼虫剂敏感性生物测定法以 1 倍区分浓度评估表型抗性,并在暴露后 24 小时记录蚊子 死亡率。通过使用诊断性 qPCR 检测筛选表型蚊子的 DNA 进行击倒抗性 (Kdr) 突变 来评估基因型抗性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 来自伊拉拉和特梅克地区的埃及伊蚊种群表现出对拟除虫菊酯和有机氯的表型抗性,成虫 死亡率 分别低于 20% 和 5%,同时仍然对有机磷酸酯和氨基甲酸酯敏感。在 Kinondoni,除氨基甲酸酯外,所有类别均观察到耐药性,并且预先接触胡椒基丁醚可使拟除虫菊酯 死亡率 平均增加 40%。F1534C 突变 在 Ilala (77%)、Kinondoni (90%) 和 Temeke (83%) 中检测到,而 V1016I 突变 频率较低。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究解释了达累斯萨拉姆地区对拟除虫菊酯和有机氯的广泛耐药性。埃及伊蚊种群,PBO 预暴露后拟除虫菊酯敏感性部分恢复表明代谢参与的证据。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了达累斯萨拉姆需要采取综合的 媒介 管理策略,包括监测抗药性趋势和评估替代杀虫剂以维持 媒介 控制有效性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于达累斯萨拉姆三个地区的表型和基因型评估,没有关于 Kdr 监测 或更广泛的生态因素之外的耐药机制的数据,需要谨慎解释和继续 监测。

title: Emerging and Re-Emerging Viral Pathogens in Oncolytic Virotherapy: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Oncolytic virotherapy has recently emerged as a promising immuno-oncological strategy, utilising the natural cytolytic potentials of viral pathogens to selectively target and destroy malignant cells. Although various engineered viruses, such as adenoviruses, vaccinia virus, and herpes simplex virus, are currently in clinical evaluation, emerging and re-emerging viruses with intrinsic oncolytic potential, including Zika virus (ZIKV), Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Dengue virus (DENV), and West Nile virus (WNV), have also shown promising results. These emerging and re-emerging viral pathogens show specific tumour tropism, immune evasion strategies, and immunogenic cell death mechanisms that could be harnessed for next-generation therapeutic platforms. Nonetheless, concerns related to safety, viral pathogenicity, host immune responses, and the risk of uncontrolled viral dissemination present significant translational challenges. The present review provides a comprehensive overview of novel viral candidates, including ZIKV, SARS-CoV-2, DENV, and WNV, in oncolytic virotherapy, their molecular mechanisms of tumour targeting, and current advancements in genetic engineering aimed at improving therapeutic efficacy and biosafety. Moreover, this review describes clinical perspectives, regulatory considerations, and future directions in integrating emerging virotherapeutic agents into precision oncology.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on dengue virus (DENV) and its role in oncolytic virotherapy, examining its tumour tropism, immune evasion strategies, and immunogenic cell death mechanisms. It also explores the potential of DENV as a therapeutic agent in the context of precision oncology.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a comprehensive analysis of emerging and re-emerging viral pathogens in oncolytic virotherapy, including DENV. It discusses the molecular mechanisms of tumour targeting and current advancements in genetic engineering to enhance therapeutic efficacy and biosafety. The review does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria for included studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Dengue virus and other related flaviviruses, such as SARS-CoV-2 and ZIKV, have shown promising oncolytic potential. These viruses possess specific tumour tropism, immune evasion strategies, and mechanisms of immunogenic cell death that could be leveraged for next-generation therapeutic platforms. The review highlights the importance of understanding these mechanisms to improve therapeutic outcomes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Safety concerns, viral pathogenicity, and host immune responses remain unresolved challenges in the use of DENV for oncolytic virotherapy. The review notes that the risk of uncontrolled viral dissemination and the need for further clinical evaluation are significant barriers to translation. Additionally, there is a lack of detailed data on the long-term effects and optimal dosing of DENV-based therapies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritise the development of genetically engineered DENV variants with enhanced therapeutic efficacy and biosafety. Clinical trials are needed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of DENV-based oncolytic virotherapy in various cancer types. Regulatory frameworks must also be established to facilitate the integration of DENV into precision oncology practices.

The review underscores the need for further research into genetic engineering of DENV to enhance therapeutic outcomes and the development of regulatory frameworks for its clinical application. These findings suggest that DENV-based therapies could be a valuable addition to precision oncology, provided that these challenges are addressed.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 登革病毒 (DENV) 及其在溶瘤病毒治疗中的作用,检查其肿瘤趋向性、免疫逃避策略和免疫原性细胞死亡机制。它还探讨了 DENV 作为精准肿瘤学背景下的治疗剂的潜力。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对溶瘤病毒疗法中新出现和重新出现的病毒病原体(包括 DENV)进行了全面分析。它讨论了肿瘤靶向的分子机制以及基因工程的最新进展,以提高治疗效果和生物安全性。该综述没有明确报告数据库、检索日期或纳入研究的资格标准。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 登革病毒 和其他相关黄病毒,例如 SARS-CoV-2 和 ZIKV,已显示出有希望的溶瘤潜力。这些病毒具有特定的肿瘤趋向性、免疫逃避策略和免疫原性细胞死亡机制,可用于下一代治疗平台。该综述强调了了解这些机制对于改善治疗结果的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 使用 DENV 进行溶瘤病毒治疗时,安全性问题、病毒致病性和 宿主 免疫应答 仍然是未解决的挑战。该评论指出,不受控制的病毒传播的风险和进一步临床评估的需要是转化的重大障碍。此外,缺乏有关 DENV 疗法的长期效果和最佳剂量的详细数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先开发具有增强治疗功效和生物安全性的基因工程 DENV 变体。需要临床试验来评估基于 DENV 的溶瘤病毒疗法在各种癌症类型中的安全性和有效性。还必须建立监管框架,以促进 DENV 融入精准肿瘤学实践。

Clinical trials are needed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of DENV-based oncolytic virotherapy in various cancer types. title_zh: 溶瘤病毒疗法中新出现和重新出现的病毒病原体:综合综述。
source_body_en: Oncolytic virotherapy has recently emerged as a promising immuno-oncological strategy, utilising the natural cytolytic potentials of viral pathogens to selectively target and destroy malignant cells. Although various engineered viruses, such as adenoviruses, vaccinia virus, and herpes simplex virus, are currently in clinical evaluation, emerging and re-emerging viruses with intrinsic oncolytic potential, including Zika virus (ZIKV), Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Dengue virus (DENV), and West Nile virus (WNV), have also shown promising results. These emerging and re-emerging viral pathogens show specific tumour tropism, immune evasion strategies, and immunogenic cell death mechanisms that could be harnessed for next-generation therapeutic platforms. Nonetheless, concerns related to safety, viral pathogenicity, host immune responses, and the risk of uncontrolled viral dissemination present significant translational challenges. The present review provides a comprehensive overview of novel viral candidates, including ZIKV, SARS-CoV-2, DENV, and WNV, in oncolytic virotherapy, their molecular mechanisms of tumour targeting, and current advancements in genetic engineering aimed at improving therapeutic efficacy and biosafety. Moreover, this review describes clinical perspectives, regulatory considerations, and future directions in integrating emerging virotherapeutic agents into precision oncology.
abstract_zh: 溶瘤病毒疗法最近成为一种有前途的免疫肿瘤学策略,利用病毒病原体的天然溶细胞潜力来选择性地靶向和破坏恶性细胞。尽管各种工程病毒,如腺病毒、牛痘病毒和单纯疱疹病毒,目前正处于临床评估阶段,但具有内在溶瘤潜力的新出现和重新出现的病毒,包括寨卡病毒(ZIKV)、严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)、登革病毒(DENV)和西尼罗河病毒(WNV)也显示出有希望的结果。这些新出现和重新出现的病毒病原体表现出特定的肿瘤趋向性、免疫逃避策略和免疫原性细胞死亡机制,可用于下一代治疗平台。尽管如此,与安全性、病毒致病性、宿主 免疫应答 以及不受控制的病毒传播风险相关的担忧提出了重大的转化挑战。本综述全面概述了溶瘤病毒治疗中的新型候选病毒,包括 ZIKV、SARS-CoV-2、DENV 和 WNV、它们的肿瘤靶向分子机制,以及旨在提高治疗效果和生物安全性的基因工程的最新进展。此外,这篇综述描述了将新兴病毒治疗药物整合到精准肿瘤学中的临床观点、监管考虑因素和未来方向。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 登革病毒 (DENV) 及其在溶瘤病毒治疗中的作用,检查其肿瘤趋向性、免疫逃避策略和免疫原性细胞死亡机制。它还探讨了 DENV 作为精准肿瘤学背景下的治疗剂的潜力。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述对溶瘤病毒疗法中新出现和重新出现的病毒病原体(包括 DENV)进行了全面分析。它讨论了肿瘤靶向的分子机制以及基因工程的最新进展,以提高治疗效果和生物安全性。该综述没有明确报告数据库、检索日期或纳入研究的资格标准。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 登革病毒 和其他相关黄病毒,例如 SARS-CoV-2 和 ZIKV,已显示出有希望的溶瘤潜力。这些病毒具有特定的肿瘤趋向性、免疫逃避策略和免疫原性细胞死亡机制,可用于下一代治疗平台。该综述强调了了解这些机制对于改善治疗结果的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 使用 DENV 进行溶瘤病毒治疗时,安全性问题、病毒致病性和 宿主 免疫应答 仍然是未解决的挑战。该评论指出,不受控制的病毒传播的风险和进一步临床评估的需要是转化的重大障碍。此外,缺乏有关 DENV 疗法的长期效果和最佳剂量的详细数据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先开发具有增强治疗功效和生物安全性的基因工程 DENV 变体。需要临床试验来评估基于 DENV 的溶瘤病毒疗法在各种癌症类型中的安全性和有效性。还必须建立监管框架,以促进 DENV 融入精准肿瘤学实践。

title: Temporal Rewiring of Innate Immunity by Vector-Borne Viruses for Host-Directed Antiviral Therapy
abstract: The geographic range and outbreak intensity of vector-borne viral infections are increasing as climate, land use, urbanization, and human mobility reshape vector ecology and human exposure. Despite their growing importance to public health, effective antiviral and preventive options remain limited for many emerging and reemerging vector-borne viruses due to viral genetic diversity, rapid evolutionary capacity, sporadic outbreak patterns, and economic constraints. While these viruses differ in taxonomy, genome organization, vector specificity, tissue tropism, and clinical manifestations, they exploit a shared vulnerability in host antiviral defense, particularly the timing of innate antiviral immunity to support viral replication, immune evasion, inflammatory dysregulation, and disease progression. Rather than simply suppressing antiviral defense, vector-borne viruses can delay early viral nucleic acid sensing, attenuate interferon induction or responsiveness, and extend the initial phase for viral replication. As viral burden increases and infected tissues undergo stress or damage, delayed immune activation can shift toward excessive inflammatory amplification, contributing to disease-specific pathology. In this study, we examine this temporal rewiring of innate antiviral immunity in representative vector-borne viruses such as dengue virus, chikungunya virus, and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus and propose that understanding these conserved host dependencies may lead to broader, stage-specific, adaptable antiviral strategies that complement conventional virus-directed approaches.

title_zh: 媒介 传播病毒对先天免疫的时间重新布线,用于 宿主 导向的 抗病毒药物 治疗
source_body_en: The geographic range and outbreak intensity of vector-borne viral infections are increasing as climate, land use, urbanization, and human mobility reshape vector ecology and human exposure. Despite their growing importance to public health, effective antiviral and preventive options remain limited for many emerging and reemerging vector-borne viruses due to viral genetic diversity, rapid evolutionary capacity, sporadic outbreak patterns, and economic constraints. While these viruses differ in taxonomy, genome organization, vector specificity, tissue tropism, and clinical manifestations, they exploit a shared vulnerability in host antiviral defense, particularly the timing of innate antiviral immunity to support viral replication, immune evasion, inflammatory dysregulation, and disease progression. Rather than simply suppressing antiviral defense, vector-borne viruses can delay early viral nucleic acid sensing, attenuate interferon induction or responsiveness, and extend the initial phase for viral replication. As viral burden increases and infected tissues undergo stress or damage, delayed immune activation can shift toward excessive inflammatory amplification, contributing to disease-specific pathology. In this study, we examine this temporal rewiring of innate antiviral immunity in representative vector-borne viruses such as dengue virus, chikungunya virus, and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus and propose that understanding these conserved host dependencies may lead to broader, stage-specific, adaptable antiviral strategies that complement conventional virus-directed approaches.
abstract_zh: 随着气候、土地利用、城市化和人类流动重塑 媒介 生态和人类暴露,媒介 传播的病毒感染的地理范围和 媒介 强度正在增加。尽管它们对公共卫生越来越重要,但由于病毒遗传多样性、快速进化能力、零星的 暴发 模式和经济限制,对于许多新出现和重新出现的 媒介 传播病毒来说,有效的 抗病毒药物 和预防方案仍然有限。虽然这些病毒在分类、基因组 组织、媒介 特异性、组织向性和临床表现方面有所不同,但它们利用了 宿主 抗病毒药物 防御中的共同弱点,特别是先天 抗病毒药物 免疫的时机,以支持病毒复制、免疫逃避、炎症失调和疾病进展。媒介携带的病毒不是简单地抑制抗病毒药物防御,而是可以延迟早期病毒核酸感应,减弱干扰素诱导或反应性,并延长病毒复制的初始阶段。随着病毒负荷的增加和受感染的组织承受压力或损伤,延迟的免疫激活可能会导致过度的炎症放大,从而导致疾病特异性病理。在本研究中,我们研究了代表性 媒介 传播病毒(例如 登革病毒、基孔肯雅病毒和严重发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒)中先天 抗病毒药物 免疫的时间重新布线,并提出了解这些保守的 宿主 依赖性可能会导致更广泛、阶段特异性、适应性强的 抗病毒药物 策略,以补充传统的病毒导向方法。

arthralgia.The condition is self-limiting and often resolves within 2 weeks. 1 Chronic illness may remain for several years, accompanied by ongoing polyarthralgia.The overlapping symptoms and shared title: Etiological Spectrum of Acute Febrile Illness in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Assam, India: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Introduction: Acute Febrile Illness (AFI) encompasses a spectrum of conditions marked by fever, often caused by various infectious agents. The aetiological diversity poses challenges in diagnosis and treatment, particularly in regions with limited diagnostic resources. Aim: To evaluate the spectrum of pathogens causing AFI with or without rash in patients. Materials and Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2024 to December 2024 on 1,544 patients who had attended Lakhimpur Medical College and Hospital, North Lakhimpur, Assam, India. Patients with fever (≥ 37.5°C) with or without rash were enrolled. Serological investigations for Measles, Rubella, Dengue, Varicella-zoster, Chikungunya viruses, Japanese Encephalitis (JE), Orientia tsutsugamushi, Leptospira, and Hepatitis viruses were performed using Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Rapid Detection Testing (RDT) kits. Data analysis was performed using both descriptive and inferential methods. A p-value of <0.05 was considered significant. Results: Fever was prevalent in all 1,544 (100%) cases, followed by 856 (55.44%) cases of headache, 636 (41.19%) with cough, 476 (30.83%) with vomiting, 347 (22.47%) with abdominal pain, 59 (3.82%) cases with dysentery, 52 (3.37%) with diarrhoea, 46 (2.98%) cases with unconsciousness, and 21 (1.36%) cases presented with rash. Fever was observed in combination with headache in 856 (55.44%), with cough in 636 (41.19%), with bodyache in 481 (31.15%), and with vomiting in 476 (30.83%) cases. The study identified seasonal variations in infection rates, with peaks during the monsoon months. The majority of positive cases were attributed to Scrub Typhus 133/817 (16.28%), followed by Leptospirosis 129/473 (27.27%), Dengue 84/1273 (6.59%), and JE 20/87 (22.99%), while some had co-infection. Conclusion: The study underscores the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches in diagnosing AFI. Scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and dengue were identified as major causes, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.
journal: Journal of Clinical and Diagnostic Research

title: Drought dynamics explain once in a century yellow fever virus outbreak in Brazil with implications for climate change
abstract: While excess rainfall is associated with mosquito-borne disease because it supports mosquito breeding, drought may also counterintuitively increase disease transmission by altering mosquito and host behavior. This phenomenon is important to understand because climate change is projected to increase both extreme rainfall and drought. In this study, we investigated the extent to which seasonally driven mosquito and primate behavior drove the first yellow fever virus (YFV) epidemic in an urban area in Brazil in nearly a century, coinciding with an equally rare drought, and assessed the role of interventions in ending the outbreak. We hypothesized that drought-like conditions played a key role in the outbreak dynamics by driving the forest mosquitoes and nonhuman primates toward the city in search of water and that the mosquitoes were biting more frequently to avoid desiccation. A dynamical YFV model supports these hypotheses, showing that both behavioral changes were needed to explain the outbreak timing and incidence. Furthermore, a combination of vector control, conservation measures, and vaccination contributed to ending the outbreak, with the strongest effects from vaccination. Together, these results suggest that drought, likely to become more frequent in this region in the coming decades, can considerably influence mosquito-borne disease transmission and that sustained control will require multiple interventions.

In this study, we investigated the extent to which seasonally driven mosquito and primate behavior drove the first yellow fever virus (YFV) epidemic in an urban area in Brazil in nearly a century, coinciding with an equally rare drought, and assessed the role of interventions in ending the outbreak. We hypothesized that drought-like conditions played a key role in the outbreak dynamics by driving the forest mosquitoes and nonhuman primates toward the city in search of water and that the mosquitoes were biting more frequently to avoid desiccation. A dynamical YFV model supports these hypotheses, showing that both behavioral changes were needed to explain the outbreak timing and incidence. Furthermore, a combination of vector control, conservation measures, and vaccination contributed to ending the outbreak, with the strongest effects from vaccination. Together, these results suggest that drought, likely to become more frequent in this region in the coming decades, can considerably influence mosquito-borne disease transmission and that sustained control will require multiple interventions.

title: Development of a potential vaccine against dengue and chikungunya virus co-infection using immunoinformatics and structural evaluation
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) co-infection poses a growing challenge in regions where both arboviruses co-circulate, highlighting the need for integrated vaccine strategies. Here, we designed a multi-epitope subunit vaccine candidate targeting conserved regions of the DENV NS1 protein and the CHIKV NSP1 protein using an immunoinformatics-based approach. Conserved CTL, HTL, and B-cell epitopes were selected on the basis of antigenicity, safety-related screening, and population coverage, then assembled with immunologically appropriate linkers and an N-terminal human β-defensin-2 adjuvant. The construct displayed favourable physicochemical features and acceptable structural quality after three-dimensional modeling and validation. Docking analysis indicated stable interaction with human TLR4, which was further examined by normal-mode analysis and 100-ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations performed in AMBER v24 with the ff19SB force field. Trajectory analyses supported conformational stability of the vaccine-TLR4 complex, and MM/GBSA calculations suggested favourable binding energetics. Codon optimization supported expression feasibility in the E. coli pET-28a(+) system. In silico immune simulation further predicted induction of both humoral and cellular immune responses, with increased antibody production and immune-memory development. These results support the proposed construct as a rational candidate for further experimental evaluation toward a vaccine strategy against DENV-CHIKV co-infection.

Conserved epitopes were selected for antigenicity, safety, and population coverage, assembled with linkers and an adjuvant, and subjected to structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations. Docking and trajectory analyses demonstrated stable interaction with human TLR4 and favourable binding energetics. In silico immune simulations predicted robust humoral and cellular immune responses, including antibody production and immune memory. The authors propose this construct as a rational candidate for further experimental evaluation against DENV-CHIKV co-infection. However, the evidence is confined to computational and in vitro predictions without animal or human validation, limiting its current scientific and public-health significance.

title: Odorant receptor coexpression and multi-expression in the dengue mosquito
abstract: Drosophila olfactory sensory neurons tend to express a single ligand-specific receptor, following a one-receptor-per-neuron rule expected to apply broadly across insects. Recent work challenges this view by showing that some neurons in the mosquito Aedes aegypti coexpress multiple receptors. However, the full extent and nature of coexpression in Ae. aegypti remains unclear. We sequenced the transcriptomes of 46,000 female antennal neurons to resolve all olfactory neuron subtypes and identify expressed receptors. Half of all subtypes coexpress multiple receptors. However, coexpression occurs almost exclusively among receptors from the same family; cross-family coexpression of odorant receptors with ionotropic receptors is rare. We also document a phenomenon called multi-expression, wherein one receptor is expressed in multiple neuron subtypes, often alongside distant paralogs. Drosophila provides rare examples of both coexpression and multi-expression, suggesting that Drosophila and Aedes are not fundamentally different, but instead located at different positions along a continuum likely to encompass diverse insects. Dengue mosquito olfactory neurons are known to show complex patterns of receptor expression, but the details of this complexity remain unclear. Here, the authors build a comprehensive molecular atlas of antennal neurons, showing that half express multiple receptors and that some receptors are expressed in multiple neurons.

abstract_original: Drosophila olfactory sensory neurons tend to express a single ligand-specific receptor, following a one-receptor-per-neuron rule expected to apply broadly across insects. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the complexity of olfactory receptor expression in the dengue mosquito, Aedes aegypti, challenging the traditional one-receptor-per-neuron rule observed in Drosophila. By sequencing the transcriptomes of 46,000 female antennal neurons, the authors resolved all olfactory neuron subtypes and identified expressed receptors. The results show that half of all subtypes coexpress multiple receptors, and some receptors are expressed in multiple neuron subtypes, often alongside distant paralogs. These findings suggest that dengue mosquitoes exhibit a similar continuum of receptor expression patterns to Drosophila, indicating a broader biological trend across insects. The study provides insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying olfactory perception in dengue mosquitoes, which could inform strategies for vector control and disease prevention. However, the study is limited to transcriptomic data and does not include functional validation, but the evidence is strong due to the comprehensive molecular atlas generated.

title: Mechanical drivers of dengue virus-induced endothelial dysfunction
abstract: More than one billion individuals worldwide are at risk of contracting dengue. Dengue virus (DENV) is a ssRNA(+)-flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. While most infections are mild (uncomplicated dengue), severe/hemorrhagic dengue carries substantial mortality and lacks specific treatment. Severe dengue is characterized by endothelial dysfunction, which can arise during both primary and secondary infection. In the latter, antibody-dependent enhancement of infection is a well-recognized risk factor, although the mechanistic links between viral infection and endothelial barrier failure remain unclear in either setting. Beyond inflammatory injury to the endothelium, DENV and other flaviviruses can trigger endothelial trans-differentiation toward a mesenchymal, migratory phenotype, weakening cell–cell junctions and compromising vascular integrity. In this review, we discuss the mechanical component of flavivirus-induced endothelial trans-differentiation and its impact on endothelial dysfunction, highlighting prospective mechanobiological targets for therapeutic intervention.

title_original: Mechanical drivers of dengue virus-induced endothelial dysfunction

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines dengue virus (DENV) infection, focusing on the mechanical drivers of endothelial dysfunction in dengue disease, particularly severe dengue, across DENV-1 to DENV-4. The central question addresses how mechanical and mechanobiological processes contribute to endothelial barrier failure during DENV infection, irrespective of primary or secondary infection contexts.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis that discusses mechanobiological mechanisms underlying DENV-induced endothelial trans-differentiation and its impact on vascular integrity. It highlights prospective mechanobiological targets for therapeutic intervention without reporting databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or included-study counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: DENV infection can induce endothelial trans-differentiation toward a mesenchymal, migratory phenotype, weakening cell–cell junctions and compromising vascular integrity. This process contributes to endothelial dysfunction, a hallmark of severe dengue, regardless of whether infection occurs during primary or secondary exposure.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The mechanistic links between DENV infection and endothelial barrier failure remain unclear, particularly regarding how antibody-dependent enhancement in secondary infections influences these processes. Additionally, the specific molecular pathways driving endothelial trans-differentiation and their relative contributions to vascular compromise are not fully resolved.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prospective mechanobiological targets for therapeutic intervention should be prioritized to mitigate endothelial dysfunction in dengue. Further research is needed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying DENV-induced endothelial trans-differentiation and its role in severe dengue pathogenesis.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the mechanical drivers of dengue virus (DENV)-induced endothelial dysfunction, a key feature of severe dengue. It highlights that DENV infection can trigger endothelial cells to adopt a mesenchymal, migratory phenotype, weakening cell–cell junctions and compromising vascular integrity. While endothelial dysfunction occurs in both primary and secondary infections, the mechanistic pathways linking DENV to barrier failure remain incompletely understood, particularly in the context of antibody-dependent enhancement. The review underscores the need for mechanobiological research to identify therapeutic targets that could prevent or reverse endothelial damage, thereby reducing the severity of dengue disease.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了 重症登革热 (DENV) 感染,重点关注登革热疾病中内皮功能障碍的机械驱动因素,特别是 DENV-1 至 DENV-4 中的 重症登革热。核心问题涉及 DENV 感染期间机械和机械生物学过程如何导致内皮屏障失效,无论原发或继发感染情况如何。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一篇叙述性综合文章,讨论了 DENV 诱导的内皮转分化的机械生物学机制及其对血管完整性的影响。它强调了治疗干预的前瞻性机械生物学目标,但没有报告数据库、检索日期、资格标准或纳入研究计数。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: DENV 感染可诱导内皮细胞向间充质迁移表型转分化,削弱细胞间连接并损害血管完整性。这一过程会导致内皮功能障碍,这是 重症登革热 的一个标志,无论感染是在初次还是二次暴露期间发生。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: DENV 感染与内皮屏障衰竭之间的机制联系仍不清楚,特别是继发感染中的 抗体依赖性增强 如何影响这些过程。此外,驱动内皮转分化的特定分子途径及其对血管损害的相对贡献尚未完全解决。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 应优先考虑治疗干预的预期机械生物学目标,以减轻登革热的内皮功能障碍。需要进一步的研究来阐明 DENV 诱导的内皮转分化的分子机制及其在 重症登革热 发病机制 中的作用。
